content.title: Company Service Model and Department Responsibilities

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Clarify departmental ownership, reporting lines and cross-department handoffs so field, dispatch and account teams act on the same approved instructions.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: Employees in Roadside, PPI, Auctions, Dispatch/VSF, Tow Truck Operations, Operations and Sales & Development. Covers assigned responsibilities, handoffs, escalation and approval boundaries.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: The company operates through Roadside, Private Property Impound (PPI), Auctions, Dispatch/VSF, Tow Truck Operators, Operations, and Sales & Development. Each department has an assigned supervisor or manager responsible for daily performance, employee expectations, and following company SOPs.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current approved instructions; records and reporting channels identified in the procedure; access limited to the assigned role.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Operations | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Department Coverage | The company operates through Roadside, Private Property Impound (PPI), Auctions, Dispatch/VSF, Tow Truck Operators, Operations, and Sales & Development. Each department has an assigned supervisor or manager responsible for daily performance, employee expectations, and following company SOPs.
02 Operational Supervision | Roadside operations are overseen by the Service Manager. PPI patrols and Tow Truck Operators are overseen by the Tow Truck Operator Supervisor. Dispatch and VSF operations are overseen by the Dispatch Supervisor. Auction work is coordinated by assigned personnel with oversight from the Director of Operations.
03 Sales and Account Handoffs | Sales Representatives are responsible for prospecting and obtaining new business, while Account Managers are responsible for existing client relationships, property check-ins, ongoing service needs, and reporting account concerns. Both Account Managers and Sales Representatives report to the Director of Sales & Development. That Director oversees sales activity, account manager performance, new account development, and maintaining client relationships. Sales and account management may not direct drivers or dispatch to change service, patrols, or enforcement without coordinating the approved change with Operations.
04 Dispatch, Driver and VSF Ownership | Dispatch owns job intake, assignment, communication, and accurate system entries. Drivers own safe field execution, required photographs, and completion of assigned work. VSF staff own vehicle custody records, release verification, and documentation. The Director of Operations oversees company-wide daily operational performance, department coordination, compliance, and resolution of issues that exceed a supervisor's authority. New accounts, service changes, or client complaints that affect field operations must be communicated between the Director of Sales & Development and the Director of Operations so the appropriate teams can carry out approved instructions.
05 Escalation and Approval | Employees should first report operational issues to their direct supervisor. Unresolved or cross-department operational issues go to the Director of Operations. Sales and account relationship issues go through the Director of Sales & Development. Matters requiring executive financial, organizational, or policy approval go to the COO, with the CEO involved when final ownership decisions are required. Immediate safety issues, serious compliance matters, and major service interruptions must be escalated without delay. Employees and supervisors may not approve exceptions outside their assigned authority.

content.title: Professional Conduct and Respectful Communication

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Provide a consistent company procedure for professional conduct and respectful communication.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: Applies to all employees in all departments. The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for professional conduct and respectful communication. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: All employees are expected to conduct themselves professionally and communicate respectfully with customers, residents, property representatives, vendors, and fellow employees. Disagreements must be handled calmly and without arguing, threatening, or making the situation worse. Threats, harassment, discrimination, intimidation, abusive language directed at others, retaliation, and other unprofessional conduct are not tolerated.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current approved instructions; records and reporting channels identified in the procedure; access limited to the assigned role.

Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Operations | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Professional Standard | All employees are expected to conduct themselves professionally and communicate respectfully with customers, residents, property representatives, vendors, and fellow employees. Disagreements must be handled calmly and without arguing, threatening, or making the situation worse. Threats, harassment, discrimination, intimidation, abusive language directed at others, retaliation, and other unprofessional conduct are not tolerated.
02 Reporting Options | Routine conduct issues should be reported to the employee's direct supervisor. If the concern involves that supervisor or the employee is uncomfortable reporting to them, the employee may contact the Director of Operations, the COO, or use the complaint form located in the employee portal. Harassment, discrimination, and retaliation complaints must follow the company's separate reporting and investigation process. Information should only be shared with those who need it to review and resolve the matter.
03 Hostile or Threatening Encounters | Employees dealing with a hostile or threatening person should avoid escalating the encounter, move to a safe location when possible, and immediately notify Dispatch or their supervisor. If there is an immediate threat to anyone's safety, contact 911. Employees should not make threats, continue unsafe confrontations, or authorize exceptions to company procedures without management approval.
04 Documentation and Review | Supervisors are responsible for documenting reported incidents, including the people involved, available evidence, actions taken, and any needed follow-up. The Director of Operations reviews operational conduct concerns and escalates serious matters to the COO when appropriate. Corrective action will be determined according to the facts, severity, and the company's existing corrective-action process.

content.title: Harassment, Discrimination and Retaliation Reporting

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Establish consistent responsibilities and steps for harassment, discrimination and retaliation reporting.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: All personnel and company-related interactions, including employees, contractors, owners, customers, vendors, property staff, residents, guests and visitors.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: Provide accessible reporting and a conflict-free review of harassment, discrimination and retaliation. Good-faith reports and participation must be protected.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Employee Portal complaint form; restricted investigation record; relevant records and witness information.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
All Personnel | Report concerns and cooperate truthfully; do not retaliate.
CEO / Uninvolved Alternate | Own an impartial investigation and limit disclosures to those who need to know.
Supervisors / Director of Operations | Receive reports, protect immediate safety and implement authorized follow-up.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Prohibited Conduct and Coverage | Sexual harassment, discrimination and retaliation are prohibited. The Company’s harassment policy covers employees, contractors, partners, customers, vendors, property-management staff, residents, guests and visitors. Unwelcome sexual advances, sexual jokes or images, unwanted physical contact, requests for sexual favors, and retaliation for rejecting advances or reporting concerns must be reported.
02 Submit a Report | Use the Google complaint form located in the Employee Portal. The form permits an anonymous report or an optional name. Anonymous reports are accepted, but limited information may restrict investigation and follow-up. A report may also be made to a supervisor, the Director of Operations or company leadership under MGT-015. An employee does not have to confront the person involved before reporting.
03 Assign a Conflict-Free Investigator | The CEO normally owns the investigation. When the complaint concerns the CEO, an owner or a founder, route it to an uninvolved COO or Director of Operations, or an independent outside reviewer such as legal counsel when necessary. A person may not investigate or decide a complaint against themselves.
04 Investigate and Protect the Reporter | Review the facts promptly and impartially, preserve evidence, and allow relevant people to respond. Use trauma-informed practices and disclose information only as needed for a fair review. Do not promise absolute secrecy. Retaliation against a good-faith reporter or participant is prohibited.
05 Resolve and Follow Up | Document the findings and authorized response. Communicate appropriate next steps to affected people, implement protective or corrective measures, and monitor for retaliation or recurrence. Substantiated misconduct is reviewed under HR-CA-022; an unsubstantiated good-faith report is not misconduct.

content.title: Paid Breaks, Personal Errands and Time Away From Work

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Provide a consistent company procedure for paid breaks, personal errands and time away from work.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: Applies to all employees in all departments. The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for paid breaks, personal errands and time away from work. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: Break and meal arrangements vary by department and position.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current approved instructions; records and reporting channels identified in the procedure; access limited to the assigned role.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Operations | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Break and Meal Arrangements | Break and meal arrangements vary by department and position. There is no single companywide lunch duration or paid/unpaid lunch arrangement. Employees must follow the break and meal schedule approved for their role and must record their time accurately using the company's approved timekeeping process. Authorized paid breaks remain on the clock. Any unpaid meal period must be uninterrupted and the employee must be completely relieved of work duties. If an employee performs work during an unpaid break, that work time must be reported and recorded.
02 Department Coverage | Dispatch and VSF personnel must coordinate break times with their supervisor to ensure continued phone, customer service, dispatch, yard and vehicle-release coverage. Tow Truck Operators and Roadside personnel must coordinate breaks around active service calls, patrol responsibilities, truck availability and necessary coverage. Office employees and management must coordinate breaks according to their approved work arrangement and departmental responsibilities.
03 Personal Errands | Employees must notify and receive approval from their supervisor before leaving their work assignment for personal errands or other non-work activities during a scheduled shift. Time away from work must be recorded correctly based on whether the employee was working, on an authorized paid break, or fully relieved of duty for unpaid time. An employee cannot leave a position uncovered or transfer responsibilities to another employee without proper coordination.
04 Emergencies and Exceptions | Personal or family emergencies will be considered on a case-by-case basis. Employees should notify their supervisor as soon as reasonably possible so coverage and timekeeping can be addressed. Department supervisors are responsible for coordinating coverage and enforcing approved arrangements. The Director of Operations oversees consistent application of this policy and reviews requests for exceptions. Specific lunch durations and paid/unpaid arrangements should be maintained in the applicable department or position instructions rather than assumed to apply to every employee.

sections.heading: Related Decisions & Boundaries
sections.text: Department-specific break schedules are not created by this policy. Unresolved benefit/attendance rules remain in ALL-004, ALL-007 and ALL-008.

content.title: Planned Time-Off Requests and Approval

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Provide a consistent company procedure for planned time-off requests and approval.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: Employees requesting planned time off, supervisors arranging coverage, and managers reviewing conflicts or exceptions. Paid-benefit eligibility is handled separately.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: Planned time-off requests must be submitted to the employee's direct supervisor at least 14 calendar days (two weeks) before the first requested day off. Employees should provide the dates requested and any information needed to arrange coverage. Submitting a request does not mean the time off has been approved. The employee must receive written confirmation from management before making arrangements that depend on being off work.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current approved instructions; records and reporting channels identified in the procedure; access limited to the assigned role.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Operations | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Submit the Request | Planned time-off requests must be submitted to the employee's direct supervisor at least 14 calendar days (two weeks) before the first requested day off. Employees should provide the dates requested and any information needed to arrange coverage. Submitting a request does not mean the time off has been approved. The employee must receive written confirmation from management before making arrangements that depend on being off work.
02 Review Coverage and Respond | The department supervisor reviews the request against scheduled coverage, staffing needs, workload, other approved absences, and the employee's assigned responsibilities. Supervisors are responsible for arranging appropriate coverage and communicating approval or denial to the employee in writing. When requests overlap, management should consider the date each request was received, the department's ability to maintain coverage, and fair treatment of employees. Requests should be reviewed in a timely manner so employees can plan accordingly.
03 Short Notice and Emergencies | A request with less than 14 days of notice may be considered as an exception when the circumstances justify it, but approval is not automatic. Unexpected illness, family emergencies, or other unplanned absences should be reported as soon as reasonably possible and handled under the separate call-out and leave procedures rather than treated as ordinary planned time off.
04 Escalate and Update the Schedule | If a supervisor cannot resolve a staffing conflict or an exception is needed, the matter goes to the Director of Operations for review. Department heads must receive approval from their appropriate executive supervisor, currently the COO when executive approval is required. Approved time off must be reflected in the department schedule and communicated to affected employees. Any paid-leave eligibility or available balance is determined under the applicable PTO and leave policy, not by approval of the requested dates alone.

sections.heading: Related Decisions & Boundaries
sections.text: Scheduling approval is separate from paid-benefit eligibility. ALL-007 remains a guidance item; this procedure does not establish benefit amounts.

content.title: PTO, Sick Days, Personal Days, Holidays and Bereavement

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Resolve the remaining decisions for pTO, sick days, personal days, holidays and bereavement before issuing an operating policy.

sections.heading: Proposed Scope
sections.text: Eligibility, accrual, use, balances, anniversary changes, holidays, rollover and separation treatment.

sections.heading: Decision to Resolve
sections.text: Resolve applicable leave-policy version and employee classifications; confirm holidays and exceptions.

sections.heading: Specific Guidance Required
sections.text:
01. The answer refers to a current approved benefit plan but does not supply the controlling eligibility, accrual, carryover, holidays, personal/sick days, waiting periods or separation terms. Earlier conversations contain versions and part-time questions, not a single reconciled issued schedule.
02. Identify the approved plan by role/classification and reconcile it with individual offers before issuing amounts. Do not convert prior proposed benefits into an entitlement.

sections.heading: Existing Source Direction — Not an Issued SOP
sections.text:
PTO, sick days, personal days, paid holidays and bereavement benefits will follow the employee's current approved benefit plan, employment agreement and applicable employee classification. Not all positions necessarily receive the same benefits. The approved plan controls eligibility, accrual rates, available hours, waiting periods, anniversary changes, carryover, payout and any other benefit terms. These amounts are not being established or changed through this SOP and must be verified against the current approved policy before being communicated to employees.
Planned PTO and personal time-off requests must be submitted to the direct supervisor at least 14 calendar days in advance and require written approval as outlined in the planned time-off SOP. Approval of time away from work does not automatically mean that the absence is paid. The supervisor must confirm department coverage, and the Director of Operations will review scheduling conflicts or exceptions beyond the supervisor's authority.
Unexpected illness and emergencies are not subject to the 14-day planned notice rule. Employees must notify their supervisor as soon as reasonably possible so work coverage can be arranged. Sick leave, bereavement and emergency absences will be reviewed according to the applicable benefit plan and any legal leave protections. Management must not treat legally protected leave as an ordinary attendance violation.
Available leave balances, hours used, and corrections should be recorded through the company's approved payroll/PTO system. Employees may request a balance review from the Director of Operations, who oversees administration and coordinates any needed corrections. Department supervisors are responsible for accurately reporting approved absences. Any proposed change to benefit eligibility, paid holidays, accrual, rollover or separation treatment requires COO approval before implementation.

content.title: Call-Outs, Shift Swaps and Uncovered Shifts

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Resolve the remaining decisions for call-outs, shift swaps and uncovered shifts before issuing an operating policy.

sections.heading: Proposed Scope
sections.text: Employee notice, manager response, replacements, approvals, unfilled shifts and documentation.

sections.heading: Issue Status
sections.text: NOT FOR OPERATIONAL ISSUE. This record preserves the proposed scope and available source direction. Unresolved details are not new permissions, requirements or disciplinary grounds.

sections.heading: Decision to Resolve
sections.text: No clear final rule: who finds coverage, who approves swaps, who must backfill, minimum staffing and on-call expectations?

sections.heading: Specific Guidance Required
sections.text:
01. Reconcile three qualifying no-shows resulting in termination with ALL-004’s three-strike wording, ALL-022’s “more than three call-ins” probation text and the discretionary HR-CA framework.
02. Clarify what counts as a call-out, an uncovered shift and a true no-call/no-show, required notice and backup contact, exceptions, protected absences, and who confirms each occurrence.

sections.heading: Existing Source Direction — Not an Issued SOP
sections.text:
Employees are responsible for reporting any inability to work an assigned shift to their direct supervisor as soon as reasonably possible. The employee must explain the affected shift and make reasonable efforts to locate another qualified employee who can cover it. A replacement or shift swap is not valid until the department supervisor approves the employee, schedule change and coverage arrangements. The supervisor remains responsible for coordinating staffing, verifying that the replacement is qualified and ensuring required operations remain covered.
Per the company's existing attendance rule, a call-out that results in an uncovered shift is considered a no-show, unless an applicable legally protected absence or management-approved emergency exception applies. Three qualifying no-shows result in termination following documented management review to verify the occurrences, circumstances, any required legal protections and approved exceptions. The Director of Operations reviews repeated attendance violations with the appropriate department supervisor and escalates termination decisions to authorized executive management. Employees must not be penalized for legally protected leave or absences that may not lawfully be treated as attendance violations.
Medical emergencies, including emergency-room visits, will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis. Supporting documentation may be requested when appropriate and legally permitted, without requiring disclosure of unnecessary private medical details. Employees should notify management as soon as reasonably possible during emergencies. An employee who does not report for a shift and fails to provide required notice is also subject to attendance review under the company's corrective-action rules.
Employees may request shift swaps, but both employees must agree and receive supervisor approval before the change takes effect. No employee may arrange coverage or exchange shifts if doing so creates overtime for the replacement without the supervisor's prior written approval. Any work actually performed must still be accurately reported and paid according to applicable law, whether the overtime was approved or not.
Uncovered shifts, denied swaps, repeated call-outs and urgent staffing shortages must be documented by the supervisor and promptly escalated to the Director of Operations when coverage cannot be secured. The Director of Operations coordinates cross-department support and any necessary executive review.
Catalogue instruction: Call outs without another employee covering the shift is considered a no show to work. After 3 no shows, the employee is terminated. In cases of emergencies such as an ER visit, a medical documentation proof will be required to not count as a call out. Employee cannot get another employee to cover their shift if that causes that other employee to get overtime without the supervisor’s approval.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: Overtime must be approved in writing by the employee's direct manager or authorized supervisor before it is worked.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Operations | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Obtain Written Approval | Overtime must be approved in writing by the employee's direct manager or authorized supervisor before it is worked. Employees are responsible for requesting this approval in advance and ensuring they receive and keep written confirmation. A verbal request, assumption that a shift needs extra coverage, or agreement between employees does not by itself authorize overtime. Supervisors are responsible for monitoring schedules, arranging coverage and reviewing requests before approving additional hours.
02 Record All Work | All employees must accurately report every hour actually worked, including early starts, late departures, interrupted breaks, emergency calls and work performed outside the normal schedule. Employees must never work off the clock or alter time records to avoid showing overtime. All compensable work time must be paid according to applicable wage-and-hour requirements even if the overtime was not authorized. Working unapproved overtime may be addressed through the company's corrective-action process, but pay for hours actually worked cannot be withheld as discipline.
03 Review Time Records | Supervisors must review time records for accuracy, identify potential overtime before it occurs when possible, and promptly communicate corrections to the Director of Operations. Timesheets and payroll corrections are due Monday by 5 PM under the established payroll cutoff. Late corrections will be reviewed for the next applicable processing cycle where permitted, without delaying any payment required by law. Employees should report missed punches or incorrect hours as soon as they are discovered.
04 Classification and Overtime Review | Overtime eligibility and calculation are based on the employee's actual duties, legally applicable classification, established workweek and wage-and-hour rules. Hourly, salaried, per-vehicle and commission compensation arrangements must each be reviewed appropriately; a pay method alone does not remove overtime obligations. The Director of Operations oversees overtime reporting, recurring unauthorized overtime, payroll corrections and staffing changes. Matters beyond delegated approval authority or requiring changes to company compensation policy are escalated to the COO.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Provide a consistent company procedure for corrective-action framework and employee expectations.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: Applies to all employees in all departments. The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for corrective-action framework and employee expectations. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment

Director of Operations | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Use the Existing Framework | The company will use its existing Corrective Action SOP Version 3.0 as the master framework for employee accountability. The established HR-CA-001 through HR-CA-043 violations and their Category 1-4 classifications must be followed and may not be replaced by a separate disciplinary system without executive approval. Supervisors must review the applicable violation, actual circumstances, available evidence, employee's active disciplinary history, intent, risk, and impact before recommending action.
02 Select a Proportionate Response | Corrective action is intended to correct performance and protect company standards, employees, customers, and operations. Depending on the circumstances, action may include documented coaching, a written warning, a final warning or performance improvement plan, restrictions or reassignment, suspension, or termination. The usual progressive process should be used when appropriate, but management is not required to repeat every step for serious misconduct. Theft, fraud, fighting, threats, harassment, falsifying records, serious safety violations, and other high-severity violations may warrant immediate escalation and stronger action under the existing framework. Existing specific policies, including attendance requirements, continue to apply subject to legal protections and proper review.
03 Confirm Approval Authority | Department supervisors are responsible for reporting and investigating concerns within their authority, verifying facts, documenting routine coaching, and recommending formal corrective action. The Director of Operations reviews formal write-ups and performance improvement expectations, checks consistency with the Version 3.0 framework, and ensures appropriate follow-up. Suspension, termination, and other major decisions requiring executive approval must be brought to the COO before final action. No supervisor may independently terminate an employee or issue discipline outside their delegated authority.
04 Complete the Record | Each formal corrective-action record must identify the applicable violation code and category, date, incident details, supporting evidence, employee's explanation, action being taken, expectations for improvement, review date when applicable, and the management approval. Employees must be given an opportunity to respond before a final decision when feasible. The employee should receive a copy and be asked to acknowledge receipt; acknowledgment does not require agreement with the findings. Refusal to sign should be documented rather than treated as proof that the incident occurred.
05 Follow Up and Protect Rights | Managers must monitor completion of required improvements and document whether expectations were met. All disciplinary records are restricted personnel information and may be accessed only by authorized management with a legitimate need to know. Complaints involving harassment, retaliation, protected leave, or other legally protected activity must be handled under the applicable separate reporting rules and cannot be punished as ordinary misconduct.

02 Secure Handling | All records must be kept in approved company systems and shared only through approved communication channels. Employees may not copy or send confidential information to personal email accounts, personal storage, social media, unauthorized outside parties, or unapproved AI tools. Drivers' licenses, license plates, tow photographs, payment information, impound records and release documents must be handled with particular care and only disclosed to persons authorized to receive them. Nothing in this SOP restricts employees from making legally protected reports or disclosures.

Business-critical systems should have an approved backup administrator or documented account-recovery procedure where supported so operations are not dependent on one individual. Employees must not disclose confidential customer information, vehicle records, account information, internal communications, or company documents through personal social media, messaging, or other unauthorized channels. Employees must follow applicable licensing, insurance, safety and company operating requirements. Any business-related passenger exception must be approved in advance by management and comply with applicable insurance and safety requirements. Visitors must have a legitimate business purpose, be approved by the appropriate supervisor, follow the company's check-in and identification requirements, and remain in permitted areas or under staff supervision. Vehicle access and releases must continue to follow the separate VSF identification, authorization and release procedures. Employees may not bring unauthorized visitors into restricted locations.

content.title: Accident, Damage, Injury and Serious-Complaint Reporting

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Provide a consistent company procedure for accident, damage, injury and serious-complaint reporting.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: Applies to all employees in all departments. The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for accident, damage, injury and serious-complaint reporting. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: All accidents, vehicle or property damage, employee injuries, safety incidents and serious customer or property complaints must be reported immediately, or as soon as it is safe to do so.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current approved instructions; records and reporting channels identified in the procedure; access limited to the assigned role.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Operations | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Immediate Reporting | All accidents, vehicle or property damage, employee injuries, safety incidents and serious customer or property complaints must be reported immediately, or as soon as it is safe to do so. Employees may not delay reporting until the next shift because damage appears minor or because they believe the company was not responsible. Reporting an incident is not an admission of fault. The first responsibility is safety: stop affected work, secure the scene when it can be done safely, obtain necessary medical assistance and call 911 for emergencies.
02 Notification and Escalation | The employee must notify their direct supervisor and Dispatch if field service, tow operations or coverage is affected. Serious incidents must also be escalated promptly to the Director of Operations. After hours, Dispatch contacts the on-duty supervisor and escalates to the Director of Operations when the incident involves injury, significant damage, a major customer complaint, unsafe equipment or an interruption of service. Incidents requiring executive attention are referred to the COO without delay. Employees and supervisors should not assume an issue has been escalated until the responsible manager has received the information.
03 Preserve the Evidence | Once the immediate situation is safe, the employee must preserve available evidence, including scene and vehicle photographs, relevant identification and contact information, witness information, dispatch and tow records, dashcam footage and other applicable system documentation. Records must be factual, accurate and retained in the approved company location. An incident or damage report must be completed as soon as reasonably practical, preferably before the end of the shift, with the supervisor responsible for confirming the report and forwarding it for review. Employees must cooperate with lawful reporting and investigation requirements and must not alter, delete or conceal evidence.
04 External Statements and Safety | Employees may provide accurate factual information and required emergency assistance, but they may not independently admit company liability, promise a refund or settlement, authorize reimbursement or repairs, or make commitments on behalf of the company without approval from authorized management. Damaged or potentially unsafe trucks and equipment must be taken out of service when necessary and may only return after appropriate evaluation and clearance.
05 Review and Close the Incident | The Director of Operations oversees incident review, documentation, insurance coordination, corrective actions and verified case closure with the relevant supervisor. Significant financial, legal or company-policy decisions are escalated to the COO or other authorized party. All incidents must be tracked through resolution, including any required customer follow-up and equipment readiness checks.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Safety Before Production | Employee safety takes priority over towing quotas, dispatch deadlines, customer demands, patrol goals and other production expectations. No employee is required to continue a task when they have a reasonable, good-faith concern that the work, vehicle, equipment, location or conditions are unsafe. Employees have the authority to stop or decline the affected task, move to a safe location when necessary, and immediately notify their direct supervisor and Dispatch if an active job or shift is affected. A good-faith safety report or use of stop-work authority must not result in retaliation.
02 Report Hazards and Fatigue | Employees must promptly report hazards, unsafe operating conditions, near misses, mechanical concerns, excessive fatigue, illness or any condition that could prevent them from safely performing assigned duties. Drivers may not continue operating a truck when fatigue or another condition makes safe driving doubtful. Employees should communicate the nature of the work-related safety concern without being required to disclose unnecessary private medical details. Serious incidents or emergencies must be handled under the accident and injury reporting SOP, including calling 911 when needed.
03 Supervisor Response | Supervisors must respond promptly, document the concern, evaluate the immediate risk and arrange safe coverage, replacement equipment, reassignment or other necessary measures. A supervisor may not direct an employee to ignore a known hazard simply to meet a performance goal. A truck, tool or other equipment with a serious safety defect must be removed from service until the issue is evaluated and corrected. Work may resume only after the hazard has been resolved or adequately controlled and an authorized, appropriately qualified person has confirmed the equipment or assignment is safe. The employee must be informed of the clearance and any applicable precautions.
04 Records and Return to Task | Safety reports, inspection findings, corrective steps, affected assignments and return-to-work or return-to-service decisions must be recorded in the approved company system. Employees are expected to cooperate with a safe reassignment or coverage instruction once the immediate risk has been addressed. Department supervisors oversee immediate response and staffing adjustments. The Director of Operations reviews unresolved or recurring hazards, ensures documentation and qualified clearance, and coordinates operational changes. Serious incidents, major resource decisions and exceptions beyond established authority are escalated to the COO without delay.

sections.heading: Existing Source Direction — Not an Issued SOP
sections.text:
Employees must report to work fit for duty and may not operate company vehicles, equipment or perform safety-sensitive responsibilities while impaired by alcohol, illegal drugs, misused medication or any other substance that affects their ability to work safely. Use, possession, distribution or impairment involving prohibited substances during work or on company property is not permitted, subject to applicable law and any approved company policy. Employees must not drive or continue hazardous work when they know their judgment, alertness, coordination or safe performance may be impaired.
Legally prescribed medication is not automatically a policy violation. Employees are responsible for reporting work-related safety limitations when medication or a medical condition may affect safe performance of essential duties. This report should be made privately to the appropriate supervisor or Director of Operations without requiring disclosure of unnecessary medical details. Management will review any restrictions, reasonable accommodation obligations and safe assignment options as applicable.
When a supervisor observes reasonable, documented signs of possible impairment, the employee must be promptly removed from driving and other safety-sensitive duties while the concern is reviewed. The supervisor must report the observable facts to the Director of Operations, preserve relevant information and arrange safe transportation or other appropriate measures when needed. An employee suspected of being impaired must not be permitted to drive a company vehicle until the safety concern has been resolved. Immediate medical emergencies require appropriate emergency assistance.
Drug or alcohol testing may be used only under the company's separately approved written testing protocol and applicable law, including any specific testing requirements that apply to a covered position. Testing triggers, procedures, providers, handling of results and any required review have not been established by this SOP and must be confirmed before implementation. A positive or disputed result must be evaluated through the applicable process rather than treated as proof of impairment without appropriate review.
Before returning to safety-sensitive duties following removal for suspected impairment, the employee must receive documented clearance from authorized management and any qualified medical or other review required under the applicable protocol. Testing, medical information and investigation records must remain confidential and restricted to those with a legitimate business need to know. Department supervisors handle immediate safety response; the Director of Operations coordinates investigation and return-to-duty review; and the COO approves major disciplinary decisions or exceptions beyond established authority. Confirmed violations are addressed under the existing Corrective Action SOP Version 3.0, with fact review and an opportunity for employee response.

Supervisors are responsible for confirming completion of departmental end-of-shift duties, correcting repeated deficiencies and documenting unresolved concerns. The Director of Operations oversees facility readiness, recurring sanitation arrangements, supply needs and larger housekeeping or security issues that require coordination across departments.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Smoking and Vaping Areas | Smoking and vaping are permitted only in outdoor areas specifically designated by management. They are prohibited inside company buildings, company vehicles, enclosed work areas, vehicle-storage spaces and any area where smoking or vaping creates a safety or fire risk. Employees may not smoke or vape near fuel, flammable products, maintenance hazards or other restricted locations. Smoking areas must be kept clean and all cigarette and vaping waste disposed of safely. Employees remain responsible for their assignments and may not leave a work area uncovered to take an unauthorized smoking break.
02 Weapons and Restricted Items | Firearms and other weapons are prohibited inside company buildings, company vehicles and restricted operating areas unless specifically authorized under a written company policy and applicable law. Any exception requires advance approval from the COO and must satisfy all applicable legal, safety and insurance requirements. No employee may display, handle, threaten another person with, or otherwise misuse a weapon while working or representing the company. Unauthorized explosives, incendiary devices and dangerous materials are not permitted in company work areas. Approved job-related tools, equipment and hazardous materials required for legitimate operations must be handled under the relevant safety procedures.
03 Locked Personal-Vehicle Exception | This policy does not prohibit a legally eligible employee from transporting or storing a lawfully possessed firearm or ammunition in the employee's locked, privately owned vehicle in an employer-provided employee parking area where protected by Texas Labor Code Sections 52.061 and 52.062. The statutory exceptions remain applicable, and this parking protection does not authorize carrying a firearm into restricted company premises or in a company-owned or leased vehicle. Employees must comply with all other applicable laws and any lawful location-specific restrictions.
04 Report and Respond | Employees must immediately report smoking or vaping in prohibited or hazardous areas, unauthorized weapons, threatening conduct, unsafe storage or suspected fire risks to their supervisor and the Director of Operations. Where a threat or immediate danger exists, employees should move to safety, avoid confrontation and contact 911. Supervisors document concerns and apply applicable site rules. The Director of Operations oversees compliance, designated smoking locations and incident follow-up. The COO approves any formal exceptions or changes to the company's weapon and restricted-item rules. Violations are reviewed under the existing corrective-action framework.

content.title: Workplace Relationships, Conflicts of Interest and Outside Solicitation

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Provide a consistent company procedure for workplace relationships, conflicts of interest and outside solicitation.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: Applies to all employees in all departments. The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for workplace relationships, conflicts of interest and outside solicitation. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: Employees must maintain professional conduct and impartial judgment in all company business.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current approved instructions; records and reporting channels identified in the procedure; access limited to the assigned role.

sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Operations | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Impartial Business Conduct | Employees must maintain professional conduct and impartial judgment in all company business. Personal relationships, family connections, outside jobs or private business interests are not automatically prohibited, but they may not interfere with safety, productivity, attendance, confidentiality, fair treatment or the employee's responsibilities to the company. Employees must disclose any actual or reasonably apparent conflict of interest to their direct supervisor or the Director of Operations as soon as it is identified. Employees may not use a personal relationship to influence assignments, hiring, scheduling, compensation, evaluations, discipline, purchasing or other company decisions.
02 Supervisory Relationships | Romantic, family or other close personal relationships involving a direct reporting or supervisory relationship must be disclosed to management so duties, reporting lines or decision-making authority can be reviewed and adjusted when necessary. A supervisor must not participate in employment decisions where a personal relationship compromises impartial judgment. The Director of Operations reviews operational conflicts and recommends appropriate safeguards or reassignment. Conflicts involving a director or senior management are referred to the COO for review. The company will consider the circumstances and business requirements rather than automatically prohibit or discipline employees solely for having a relationship.
03 Outside Interests and Solicitation | Outside employment and independent business activities are generally permitted when they do not interfere with scheduled work, employee fitness for duty, company obligations or the confidentiality of company information. Employees must disclose outside financial interests, vendor relationships, referral arrangements or other activities that could affect a company decision. Employees may not solicit unauthorized gifts, payments, referral fees, kickbacks or personal benefits in exchange for company business or favorable treatment. They may not secretly divert company customers, property accounts, leads, business opportunities, or resources for personal gain while carrying out their company duties, or misuse company customer lists, pricing, contracts or confidential records for outside purposes. This policy does not prohibit lawful outside activity or legally protected employee communications about pay, working conditions or other rights.
04 Review and Safeguards | Department supervisors must promptly report possible conflicts and maintain the confidentiality of disclosures to the extent practical. The Director of Operations coordinates investigations and operational safeguards, including any needed involvement of the Director of Sales & Development for client, account management or sales-related concerns. The COO reviews conflicts involving management, material financial interests and exceptions beyond delegated authority. Confirmed misconduct is handled under the existing Corrective Action SOP Version 3.0 after fact review and an opportunity for the employee to respond.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Provide a consistent company procedure for company cards, purchasing and reimbursement requests.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: Applies to all employees in all departments. The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for company cards, purchasing and reimbursement requests. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: Employees may only use a company credit or debit expense card after signing the required card authorization agreement and receiving approval for the assigned card and spending limit.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment

Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Operations | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Card Authorization and Limits | Employees may only use a company credit or debit expense card after signing the required card authorization agreement and receiving approval for the assigned card and spending limit. Card limits are established according to the employee's job duties and anticipated purchasing needs. The funds needed to support the requested limit must be available in the company's checking account before that limit is established. Employees must use company cards only for legitimate, authorized business expenses and remain within their approved limits and department budget.
02 Purchase Approval | Purchases require approval from the appropriate department supervisor or other authorized manager before funds are spent. Unusual purchases, expenses exceeding an employee's authority, and requests outside the department budget must be escalated for additional approval. If an urgent operational need makes advance approval impractical, the employee must contact management as soon as reasonably possible, limit any spending to what is necessary and document the reason for the emergency. Emergency circumstances do not authorize unrestricted spending or bypass required review.
03 Receipts and Reconciliation | Every purchase must be supported by an itemized receipt and an explanation of the business purpose, submitted through the approved expense process. Supervisors verify that purchases were necessary, authorized and correctly categorized. Lost receipts, suspected card misuse, inaccurate charges or disputed transactions must be reported immediately to the supervisor and Director of Operations. Company cards may not be used for personal purchases, cash advances or other unauthorized transactions.
04 Reimbursement Requests | The Director of Operations administers employee mileage and business-expense reimbursements. Approved business mileage is reimbursed using the applicable IRS standard mileage rate and must include adequate mileage and trip documentation. Expense and mileage reimbursement forms are due Monday by 5 PM for payment in the following applicable payroll cycle under the existing company process. Submissions received after that cutoff are considered in the subsequent reimbursement cycle, subject to any earlier payment requirement imposed by law. Employees should not be expected to personally fund company purchases when an approved company purchasing method is available.
05 Misuse Review and Recovery Limits | Unauthorized purchases, missing documentation or suspected misuse are reviewed under the existing corrective-action framework. These circumstances do not automatically authorize deductions from wages. Any recovery or payroll deduction requires applicable legal authority and any legally required written employee authorization. Department supervisors review routine requests; the Director of Operations oversees expense records, reimbursements and investigations; and the COO establishes department budgets and approves major spending exceptions or changes to company purchasing rules.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Use the Current SOP | All employees are responsible for following the current, approved Standard Operating Procedures applicable to their position and department. Approved SOPs are the company's official work instructions and must be used during onboarding, daily operations, training, corrective coaching and performance review. Drafts, outdated copies and informal messages do not replace an approved procedure. When an SOP is unclear, appears outdated, conflicts with another instruction or does not address an actual operating condition, employees must notify their direct supervisor and request clarification before proceeding when practical. No employee is expected to follow an instruction that creates an immediate safety hazard or requires a violation of applicable law; such concerns must be promptly escalated under the safety and stop-work reporting process.
02 Recommend and Route Changes | Employees and supervisors are encouraged to recommend improvements, but they may not independently revise, waive or publish company SOP requirements. Proposed changes must be submitted through the appropriate department head to the Director of Operations, with an explanation of the problem, proposed correction and affected roles or systems. Department heads review the operational impact and verify that the recommendation is compatible with safety, licensing, customer agreements and other company requirements. The Director of Operations coordinates cross-department review, maintains the official master SOP library and tracks drafts, approvals, effective dates and revisions. The Director of Sales & Development reviews proposed changes affecting sales representatives, account managers or property accounts.
03 Approve and Control Revisions | New companywide SOPs, material policy changes and exceptions outside delegated departmental authority require approval by the COO before taking effect. Once approved, the official version must identify its SOP number or title, version, effective date, approving authority and a summary of the changes. Superseded versions must be archived for reference, and employees must be directed to the current approved source. Draft or pending guidance must be clearly labeled and must not be represented as an operative policy. A material change must be communicated to affected departments before enforcement, with additional training when necessary.
04 Training and Acknowledgment | Employees must acknowledge applicable SOPs during onboarding and whenever a substantive update affects their duties. Supervisors are responsible for confirming that employees received the updated instructions, understood their responsibilities and completed any required competency or training review. Acknowledgments, training records, approval history and prior versions must be maintained in the approved company records. The Director of Operations coordinates a formal review of the SOP library at least annually and requests interim reviews after significant operational changes, serious incidents, compliance updates or recurring process failures. Unresolved questions or urgent exceptions are escalated to the COO through the Director of Operations.

content.title: Pay Questions, Payroll Corrections and Document Requests

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Provide a consistent company procedure for pay questions, payroll corrections and document requests.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: Applies to all employees in all departments. The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for pay questions, payroll corrections and document requests. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: Employees must direct questions regarding their pay, missing hours, incorrect rates, commissions, deductions, paystubs, tax forms or other payroll documents to the Director of Operations, who administers the company's payroll process.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current approved instructions; records and reporting channels identified in the procedure; access limited to the assigned role.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Operations | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Raise a Pay Question | Employees must direct questions regarding their pay, missing hours, incorrect rates, commissions, deductions, paystubs, tax forms or other payroll documents to the Director of Operations, who administers the company's payroll process. Suspected errors must be reported promptly in writing and should identify the employee, affected work dates or pay period, the amount or hours in question, and any supporting time records or other relevant documentation. Employees may first obtain assistance from their direct supervisor, but may also report a concern directly to the Director of Operations. Payroll questions must be treated professionally and reviewed without retaliation.
02 Monday Input Cutoff | All timesheets, time corrections and routine payroll adjustments are due by Monday at 5:00 PM, consistent with the company's established payroll cutoff. Requests received after that time are ordinarily reviewed for the subsequent payroll processing cycle rather than the upcoming cycle. This administrative cutoff does not permit the company to omit hours actually worked, delay wages beyond applicable legal deadlines, or disregard an obligation to issue a timely correction or other payment required by law. Employees must record all hours actually worked accurately, whether or not the work or overtime was authorized in advance. Supervisors are responsible for promptly reviewing reported hours, attendance discrepancies, commissions and other departmental inputs, verifying supporting records and forwarding corrections to the Director of Operations.
03 Review and Correct | The Director of Operations must review requests against approved timekeeping records, compensation terms and available supporting information; identify any needed supervisor or management approval; document the finding; and communicate the disposition to the employee. Disputed compensation terms, significant adjustments, suspected improper deductions or unresolved discrepancies must be escalated to the COO for review when they exceed normal payroll authority. Employees must not independently edit approved payroll records or attempt to resolve a discrepancy by changing the underlying time worked. All corrections and approvals must be recorded in the company's authorized payroll or personnel records.
04 Paystubs, Tax Forms and Privacy | Employees may access and download paystubs through their designated payroll employee portal. Employees who cannot access a paystub should contact the Director of Operations for account assistance or a copy. Employees are responsible for maintaining their correct mailing address and other required information on file; annual W-2 forms will be provided by the applicable legal deadline through the company's approved process. Employees should examine their paystubs and promptly report known concerns, preferably before year-end when practicable. Payroll, tax, identity and banking information must be transmitted and retained through approved secure channels and disclosed only to individuals who need access to perform their duties. Nothing in this procedure restricts employees from discussing their own wages or exercising other legally protected rights.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: Slack is the company's designated channel for routine internal updates, including daily progress, patrol and assignment updates, operational coordination, nonurgent questions, shift handoffs and follow-up on completed tasks.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current approved instructions; records and reporting channels identified in the procedure; access limited to the assigned role.

sections.heading: Responsibilities

Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Operations | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Routine Slack Updates | Slack is the company's designated channel for routine internal updates, including daily progress, patrol and assignment updates, operational coordination, nonurgent questions, shift handoffs and follow-up on completed tasks. Employees must use their authorized company accounts and the approved workspace and channels applicable to their department. Supervisors are responsible for identifying the correct recipients, monitoring work-related updates and ensuring that assignments and handoffs are understood. Communication must be accurate, professional, timely and limited to employees who have a legitimate need for the information. Employees should not assume that posting a message confirms it has been received or acted upon.
02 Urgent Telephone Escalation | Urgent or safety-related issues require an immediate telephone call to the responsible supervisor or on-duty manager; a Slack message, direct message or email by itself is not an acceptable emergency escalation. Employees must call immediately for accidents, injuries, unsafe towing conditions, serious customer or property-management complaints, threats, security incidents, truck breakdowns affecting service, vehicle-storage or release disruptions, or any significant failure that compromises dispatch, coverage or operations. Drivers must also notify Dispatch promptly whenever an active assignment, truck availability or service coverage is affected. Emergencies requiring police, fire or medical assistance must be reported to 911 as appropriate before or alongside company notification.
03 Coverage and Backup Contacts | During after-hours operations, Dispatch contacts the on-duty supervisor and follows the approved escalation directory. If the initial contact does not answer or the problem remains unresolved, the employee or dispatcher must immediately continue to the next authorized contact rather than wait for a Slack reply. Serious matters and unresolved operating risks are escalated to the Director of Operations, with executive-level incidents referred to the COO. The approved contact directory must identify the current phone numbers, on-call assignments, backup contacts and escalation order; this SOP does not establish unconfirmed Slack channel names or arbitrary response-time thresholds.
04 Accurate Handoffs | After an urgent situation is stabilized, the responsible employee must document the issue, actions taken, contacts notified, outstanding tasks and required follow-up in the approved incident, dispatch or company communication system. Outgoing staff must provide a clear handoff of unresolved matters, scheduled assignments and immediate priorities to incoming personnel and the relevant supervisor. Confidential customer records, payroll or medical information, passwords and other restricted data must not be posted in general Slack channels; approved secure systems must be used for sensitive information. Department supervisors enforce routine communication and handoff expectations. The Director of Operations maintains the operational escalation procedures and communication standards, coordinates cross-department issues and refers major exceptions to the COO.

content.title: Unexpected Illness, Contagious Symptoms and Return to Work

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Provide a consistent company procedure for unexpected illness, contagious symptoms and return to work.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: Applies to all employees in all departments. The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for unexpected illness, contagious symptoms and return to work. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: Employees who become unexpectedly ill, experience potentially contagious symptoms or cannot safely perform an assigned shift must notify their direct supervisor as soon as reasonably possible, preferably before the scheduled start time.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current approved instructions; records and reporting channels identified in the procedure; access limited to the assigned role.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Operations | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Illness Notification | Employees who become unexpectedly ill, experience potentially contagious symptoms or cannot safely perform an assigned shift must notify their direct supervisor as soon as reasonably possible, preferably before the scheduled start time. The employee should identify the affected shift, expected availability and any immediate staffing or safety concern. An illness or emergency does not fall under the 14-day advance notice requirement for planned time off. Employees must follow the company's existing call-out and attendance procedure, including making reasonable efforts to identify qualified coverage when circumstances permit. The department supervisor remains responsible for approving replacements and coordinating coverage, and employees are not required to put their health or safety at risk to report to work.
02 Safe Coverage and Handoff | Employees who are experiencing symptoms that could expose others to illness or compromise safe job performance must promptly advise their supervisor and follow applicable workplace health guidance and instructions. Employees who become sick during a shift must immediately notify the supervisor and Dispatch when operational coverage is affected. Drivers and employees assigned to other safety-sensitive duties must stop the affected work when illness, dizziness, weakness or similar symptoms prevent safe performance. Management must arrange qualified replacement coverage, safe transportation when necessary and appropriate operational handoffs. Employees should not disclose diagnoses or personal medical details in general Slack channels or other public work communications.
03 Documentation and Return to Work | When appropriate and legally permitted, management may request reasonable supporting documentation regarding an absence, work restriction or return-to-duty clearance. A doctor's note is not automatically required for every illness, and requests must be handled consistently with applicable law and the circumstances. Medical records and health-related information must be kept confidential and limited to personnel with a legitimate need to know. Return to work must be based on the employee's ability to safely perform required duties, applicable workplace health guidance, any legally required accommodations or leave protections, and qualified medical clearance where reasonably necessary for safety-sensitive work. The Director of Operations coordinates restrictions, any temporary reassignment and required return-to-work review with the responsible supervisor.
04 Protected Absences and Escalation | Illness-related absences are subject to the existing attendance, call-out and uncovered-shift procedures, including the company's documented no-show review, except where legally protected leave, a management-approved emergency exception or other applicable protections require different treatment. No absence may be counted as a qualifying no-show or disciplined without reviewing the facts, applicable protections and documented exceptions. Employees must not be retaliated against for exercising protected leave rights or reporting legitimate health-related safety concerns. Supervisors document notices, coverage efforts and attendance issues without recording unnecessary private health details. The Director of Operations reviews unresolved coverage problems and return-to-work restrictions; significant exceptions or proposed termination decisions are escalated to the COO for approval.

content.title: PPE Availability, Proper Use, Care and Replacement

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Resolve the remaining decisions for pPE availability, proper use, care and replacement before issuing an operating policy.

sections.heading: Proposed Scope
sections.text: Role-specific protective equipment, condition checks, access, replacement and training. Any missing or low stock PPE supplies must be reported.

sections.heading: Issue Status
sections.text: NOT FOR OPERATIONAL ISSUE. This record preserves the proposed scope and available source direction. Unresolved details are not new permissions, requirements or disciplinary grounds.

sections.heading: Decision to Resolve
sections.text: Role/equipment requirements, issue/replacement authority and employee costs separate from extra uniforms.

sections.heading: Specific Guidance Required
sections.text:
01. The answer provides a general PPE framework, but the question asks for actual role/equipment requirements. Supply the task-specific PPE matrix, issue/replacement owner and approved training/checklist.
02. Do not treat general PPE wording as a technical towing, electrical, roof-access or traffic-exposure work procedure. Current stop-work and supply-reporting expectations remain in ALL-016 and OPS-007.

sections.heading: Existing Source Direction — Not an Issued SOP
sections.text:
All employees are required to use the personal protective equipment (PPE) appropriate for their assigned duties, workplace conditions and identified hazards. Department supervisors must assess the tasks performed by their teams, identify required protective equipment, confirm proper fit and availability, and ensure employees understand when and how it must be used. Towing and roadside personnel must use appropriate protective equipment for traffic exposure, vehicle recovery, load securement, equipment operation and related hazardous work. Yard, maintenance, dispatch and other employees must follow the PPE requirements applicable to their tasks. Required PPE and task-specific safety precautions must be included in employee training and relevant operating checklists.
The company must provide PPE required under applicable workplace safety standards at no cost to employees where required by law, including ordinary replacement of employer-paid PPE. Any legally recognized exceptions, such as certain non-specialty personal footwear or eyewear, must be evaluated under the applicable rule rather than assumed. Required safety equipment is separate from optional uniforms, extra uniform purchases and ordinary clothing. No employee may be required to purchase employer-paid PPE or have unauthorized charges or deductions imposed for required protective equipment. Any question about lost or intentionally damaged equipment, replacement costs or legally permitted exceptions must be reviewed by the Director of Operations before a decision is made.
Employees must inspect assigned PPE before use, wear and use it as instructed, maintain it in a sanitary and serviceable condition, and store it safely when not in use. Employees may not remove, modify, disable or misuse protective equipment required for a task. Missing, damaged, excessively worn, improperly fitting or otherwise unsuitable PPE must be reported immediately to the direct supervisor, and the affected work must not proceed until appropriate protective equipment is available and the task can be performed safely. Drivers must include required PPE availability and condition in their pre-shift truck inspection before leaving the yard. Supervisors must arrange replacement equipment or a safe reassignment rather than pressure employees to work without required protection.
Employees must also report PPE supplies that are missing or running low before inventory is exhausted. Supervisors are responsible for monitoring stock, documenting equipment issuance or replacement when appropriate, coordinating restocking and verifying compliance during routine inspections. PPE training must be refreshed when equipment or hazards change or when an employee demonstrates a need for additional instruction. The Director of Operations oversees PPE purchasing, replacement approvals, training records, recurring compliance issues and escalations beyond departmental authority. Serious hazards and unresolved supply failures must be addressed under the company's safety and stop-work procedures, with significant exceptions referred to the COO.
