content.title: Software Issue Reporting and Urgent System-Failure Escalation

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Provide a consistent company procedure for software issue reporting and urgent system-failure escalation.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: Applies to all employees in all departments. The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for software issue reporting and urgent system-failure escalation. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: Employees must promptly report software errors, account or login failures, missing or inaccurate records, equipment connectivity problems and suspected system outages that affect company work.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current approved instructions; records and reporting channels identified in the procedure; access limited to the assigned role.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Operations | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Report the Issue | Employees must promptly report software errors, account or login failures, missing or inaccurate records, equipment connectivity problems and suspected system outages that affect company work. Routine issues that do not materially interrupt service must be submitted through the approved software issue reporting process, with the affected system, employee or department, approximate time, task being performed, error message and steps already attempted. Screenshots, logs or other supporting information should be included when useful and permitted, but employees must not expose passwords, security codes, confidential customer records or other restricted information in general communication channels.
02 Escalate Critical Failures | An issue is operationally critical when it prevents or seriously compromises Dispatch, active towing assignments, vehicle-storage or release operations, required safety documentation, access to essential records, or another time-sensitive service. Critical failures must be reported immediately by telephone to the direct supervisor or on-duty manager; a Slack message or routine issue ticket alone is not sufficient. Drivers must also advise Dispatch if active assignments or service coverage are affected. After hours, Dispatch follows the approved on-call escalation directory, contacting the on-duty supervisor and escalating unresolved or significant outages to the Director of Operations. Major interruptions, security incidents or substantial financial exposure are referred to the COO. If the initial contact is unavailable, employees must continue through the approved backup contact sequence rather than wait for a written response.
03 Authorized Troubleshooting | Employees may perform only troubleshooting steps within their training and assigned system permissions. They may not disable security controls, share credentials, independently alter or recreate company records, install unapproved software, or invent manual processes to bypass compliance requirements. Department supervisors coordinate approved workarounds, qualified coverage and safe business continuity arrangements. Any temporary paper process or alternative system must be specifically authorized, protect required records, and include a documented plan for entering or reconciling information when normal service is restored. Only designated system administrators, approved technical support personnel or other authorized staff may perform restricted configuration changes or restore elevated access.
04 Reconcile and Verify Recovery | The supervisor or issue owner must document the reported condition, operational impact, priority, contacts notified, corrective steps, temporary measures, assigned follow-up and verified resolution in the approved system. Affected personnel must be informed when the system is restored and any pending transactions or records require reconciliation. The Director of Operations coordinates recurring system issues, critical service recovery and cross-department follow-up, with executive-level decisions escalated to the COO. Current support contacts, approved workspace or ticket channels, system-specific recovery procedures and response targets must be maintained in the official support directory; unconfirmed details are not established by this SOP.

content.title: Shared Accountability & Error Reporting

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Protect the Company’s licensure, integrity, people and customer property by catching errors early, reporting concerns and correcting problems as a team. One person’s mistake can expose the entire Company to risk.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: This SOP applies to all employees, contractors, supervisors, managers and working owners in every department. It covers work performed, received, reviewed or observed during Company operations.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text:
Everyone has a duty to double-check one another’s work and speak up when an error, omission, accident or unsafe practice is discovered. Friendships, family relationships, job titles and department boundaries do not excuse ignoring or concealing a concern.
Report concerns in good faith, even when all facts are not yet known. A respectful report is not disloyalty or insubordination. Retaliation is prohibited. If you fear retaliation, tell your supervisor; if the concern involves your supervisor, contact any other supervisor or manager. You do not need that supervisor’s permission.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current SOPs and checklists; relevant records within authorized access; a supervisor or manager contact; and approved reporting tools, including the Employee Portal complaint form.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
All Personnel | Check work, report concerns promptly, preserve relevant records and cooperate truthfully. Receive corrections professionally.
Supervisors & Managers | Receive reports without retaliation, control immediate risk, arrange a fair review, assign corrective follow-up and verify completion.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Check & Protect | Compare the work with the applicable SOP or checklist. Flag missing, inaccurate or unsafe work. Pause an unsafe activity when safe to do so and notify supervision. Call 911 for an immediate emergency.
02 Report & Escalate | Tell your supervisor what you observed and what may be affected. Report urgent safety, damage or compliance concerns immediately. Do not delay reporting while trying to prove fault or quietly fix the issue.
03 Raise Retaliation Concerns | State any fear of retaliation. Bypass an involved or unavailable supervisor and contact any other supervisor or manager. The Employee Portal complaint form is another route; anonymous reports may limit follow-up.
04 Document & Preserve | Record the date, time, task, observed issue, people notified and immediate action. Preserve original photos, messages and records. Do not delete, hide, backdate or falsify evidence, or access restricted records without authorization.
05 Review & Close | Management reviews the facts fairly, assigns the correction and checks completion. A concern involving a supervisor must be routed to another appropriate manager. Escalate again if the issue remains unresolved or retaliation occurs.

sections.heading: Definitions & Abbreviations
sections.text: ALL: All Personnel. SAER: Shared Accountability & Error Reporting. SOP: Standard Operating Procedure. HR-CA: Human Resources – Corrective Action. Good Faith: An honest concern, even if not substantiated. Retaliation: Threats, intimidation or adverse treatment because someone reported or assisted a review.

sections.heading: Corrective Action References
sections.text:
Reference | When It Applies | Category
HR-CA-016, HR-CA-028 | Failure to follow required checks; paperwork or data-entry errors. | 1, 2 or 3
HR-CA-018, HR-CA-020 | Failure to report serious incidents; falsifying or concealing records. | 3 or 4
HR-CA-022 | Harassment, discrimination or retaliation. | 4
HR-CA-032 | Safety violations or continuing after a serious hazard is known. | 3 or 4
Good-faith reporting is not misconduct. Any underlying error is reviewed separately. Document ALL-031 with the applicable HR-CA reference; use the master guide for the final category and response. Respectful safety reporting is not insubordination (HR-CA-024).

content.title: Screening, Credentials and Onboarding Approvals

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Resolve the remaining decisions for screening, credentials and onboarding approvals before issuing an operating policy.

sections.heading: Proposed Scope
sections.text: Background/drug checks, role licenses, original-document verification and offer approval.

sections.heading: Issue Status
sections.text: NOT FOR OPERATIONAL ISSUE. This record preserves the proposed scope and available source direction. Unresolved details are not new permissions, requirements or disciplinary grounds.

sections.heading: Decision to Resolve
sections.text: Vendor/process standards, clearance timing and current official requirements; preserve protected information.

sections.heading: Specific Guidance Required
sections.text:
01. The general current answer is usable as a screening framework but defers the actual role-specific checklist, approved provider and testing protocol. Attach the adopted requirements and release-to-duty signoff before treating onboarding as complete.
02. The older onboarding sheet automatically rejects any theft record; the current workbook requires individualized authorized review and applicable notices. Reconcile the documents explicitly.
03. Replace the older I-9 instruction that directs specific documents with an approved process respecting employee choice among acceptable documents; the current workbook already requires lawful verification.

sections.heading: Existing Source Direction — Not an Issued SOP
sections.text:
All candidates and new employees must complete the screening and credential verification required for their specific position before being cleared to perform independent duties that depend on those qualifications. Screening requirements are determined by the role, applicable law, insurance obligations and approved company hiring procedures rather than a single universal checklist. The responsible department supervisor identifies the position's qualifications and submits the candidate's documentation for review. The Director of Operations coordinates completion and maintains the onboarding clearance record. Hiring decisions, conditional offers and exceptions requiring executive authority must be approved by the COO or another expressly authorized hiring decision-maker.
Background checks, reference checks and any other employment screening must be conducted through an approved process and, where applicable, an authorized provider. Required candidate notices, written permissions, verification steps, individualized review, and any pre-adverse or adverse-action procedures must be followed before an employment decision is finalized. Screening information may be used only for legitimate job-related purposes and must not be the basis for prohibited discrimination or inconsistent treatment. Employees may not independently reject a candidate, bypass review requirements or represent a screening result as a final hiring decision without authorization.
The company must verify required licenses, towing credentials, driving qualifications, applicable certifications, work eligibility and any other job-specific qualifications using appropriate official sources or legally acceptable original documents. Employment eligibility verification must be completed through the required process and within applicable deadlines, without demanding documents beyond those legally permitted. A driver may not operate company towing equipment independently until the necessary licensing, insurance eligibility, required training and operational clearance have been confirmed. Dispatch, VSF, office, sales and management roles must likewise meet the credentials and access requirements relevant to their duties. Conditional offers must clearly identify any remaining qualifications or approvals and may not be treated as unrestricted clearance to work.
Drug or alcohol screening must be carried out only where legally required or permitted and under the company's separately approved written testing protocol. This SOP does not establish unconfirmed screening vendors, testing triggers, collection methods, review procedures or return-to-duty standards. Any questionable result or missing qualification must be referred to the Director of Operations for appropriate review before further action.
Background reports, identification records, medical or testing information and other sensitive candidate documents must be protected in authorized company systems with access limited to personnel who have a legitimate need to know. The responsible supervisor confirms role training and practical readiness; the Director of Operations verifies required documentation and records the clearance status before independent duties are assigned. Unresolved screening concerns, disputed findings, conditional-offer changes and major exceptions must be escalated to the COO for an authorized employment decision. All approvals and outstanding requirements must be documented in the restricted onboarding record.

content.title: Investigations, Corrective Actions and Write-Up Completion

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Provide a consistent company procedure for investigations, corrective actions and write-up completion.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for investigations, corrective actions and write-up completion. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: All investigations, employee write-ups and formal corrective actions must follow the company's existing Corrective Action SOP Version 3.0.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current approved instructions; records and reporting channels identified in the procedure; access limited to the assigned role.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Operations | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Use the HR-CA Framework | All investigations, employee write-ups and formal corrective actions must follow the company's existing Corrective Action SOP Version 3.0. The approved HR-CA-001 through HR-CA-043 violation codes and Category 1 through Category 4 classifications remain the controlling framework. Supervisors and managers may not substitute a different violation scale, create an independent discipline ladder or change a category without the required executive approval. The type and severity of a proposed action must reflect the applicable code, facts of the incident, employee's active disciplinary history, intent, safety or customer impact, and any legally protected circumstances.
02 Gather Facts and Evidence | When a concern is reported, the responsible department supervisor must promptly secure relevant evidence, identify involved employees and witnesses, review available operating records, and document the incident using factual, objective descriptions. Evidence may include time records, dispatch or tow records, photographs, system logs, customer communications and witness statements as appropriate. Employees must not be directed to alter, conceal or delete records. The employee concerned must be given a reasonable opportunity to explain what occurred before a final determination when feasible. Allegations involving a supervisor, harassment, retaliation, protected leave or another conflict of interest must be escalated for an impartial review rather than investigated solely by the person implicated.
03 Review and Obtain Approval | Supervisors may provide documented routine coaching and recommend formal corrective action within their delegated authority. The Director of Operations reviews formal write-ups before they are finalized, verifies the appropriate HR-CA code and category, checks supporting evidence and consistency with the approved framework, and confirms any necessary approvals. Written or final warnings, performance improvement requirements, temporary restrictions, reassignment, suspension and termination must follow the authority assigned under Version 3.0 and the company's approval hierarchy. Suspension, termination and other major disciplinary decisions require COO approval before final action. No department supervisor may independently terminate an employee or issue an action beyond their authority. Serious misconduct, including theft, fraud, threats, fighting, harassment, falsification of records or major safety violations, may require immediate protective measures and executive review without repeating every progressive discipline step.
04 Complete the Write-Up | Every formal write-up must include the incident date, specific conduct or performance concern, applicable HR-CA violation code and category, relevant evidence, employee response, prior active actions considered, the action approved, corrective expectations, deadlines or review dates where appropriate, and the name of the approving manager. The employee must be offered a copy and asked to acknowledge receipt; acknowledgment confirms receipt only and does not require agreement. If the employee declines to sign, management documents the refusal without treating it as proof of misconduct. The employee may submit a written response or use the approved complaint and appeal process.
05 Monitor and Retain | Supervisors are responsible for monitoring required improvement and documenting follow-up results. The Director of Operations coordinates consistent application, review and restricted retention of corrective-action records. Access is limited to authorized personnel with a legitimate business need to know, and unresolved appeals or significant disputed findings are escalated through the applicable management process to the COO when required.

sections.text: Apply normal categories and any permitted fact-based adjustment through the authorized review in the HR-CA framework. Changing the company’s framework itself requires executive approval.

content.title: Performance Improvement, Final Warnings and Termination Review

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Provide a consistent company procedure for performance improvement, final warnings and termination review.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for performance improvement, final warnings and termination review. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: Performance improvement plans, final warnings and termination recommendations must follow the company's existing Corrective Action SOP Version 3.0.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current approved instructions; records and reporting channels identified in the procedure; access limited to the assigned role.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Operations | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Select the Appropriate Process | Performance improvement plans, final warnings and termination recommendations must follow the company's existing Corrective Action SOP Version 3.0. The approved HR-CA-001 through HR-CA-043 violation codes and their Category 1 through Category 4 classifications remain in effect; this procedure does not replace them or create a separate disciplinary ladder. The appropriate action must be determined from the specific conduct or performance concern, documented facts, prior active corrective actions, safety and operational impact, and applicable employment protections. Progressive discipline should be considered when appropriate, but no employee is automatically entitled to every step before a serious matter is escalated.
02 Build a Measurable PIP | A performance improvement plan (PIP) may be used when an employee has a correctable deficiency in productivity, quality, attendance, job knowledge, required procedures or other measurable expectations. The supervisor must describe the deficiency with specific examples, identify the required improvement, establish measurable and reasonable targets, identify any training or resources to be provided, and set the review dates and completion criteria. The improvement period must be appropriate to the position and concern; there is no universal PIP length established by this SOP. The employee must be informed of the expectations, potential consequences if improvement is not achieved, and how progress will be evaluated. The employee should have an opportunity to respond, receive a copy of the plan and acknowledge receipt. A refusal to sign is documented but does not establish agreement or misconduct.
03 Document Progress | During the improvement period, the direct supervisor must conduct and record regular progress check-ins, provide any approved coaching or support, and document objective results against the stated criteria. Successful completion must be confirmed in writing and may be followed by continued reasonable performance monitoring. If expectations are not met, the supervisor must summarize the results, supporting records and employee explanation, and submit a recommendation to the Director of Operations for review. Any extension, revised target, final warning or further action must be documented and approved under the applicable authority and Version 3.0 classification; targets must not be changed retroactively to manufacture a failure.
04 Review Serious Action | Final written warnings may be appropriate for repeated deficiencies or more serious violations under the approved corrective-action framework. Serious misconduct, including theft, threats, harassment, falsification of records and major safety violations, may require immediate protective action and COO review without first issuing a PIP. Before a termination recommendation is finalized, the Director of Operations must review the investigation, applicable HR-CA code and category, active disciplinary history, documented improvement efforts, consistency of treatment, the employee's response and any protected leave, accommodation, retaliation or other legal concern. Department supervisors may recommend but may not independently approve termination. Termination, suspension and other major decisions requiring executive authorization must be approved by the COO before implementation.
05 Maintain Restricted Records | All PIPs, coaching notes, formal warnings, review meetings, employee responses, approvals and final dispositions must be preserved in restricted personnel records. Employees may raise disagreements through the approved complaint and appeal procedure. The Director of Operations coordinates follow-up, documentation and consistency across departments; the COO retains final executive authority for major disciplinary decisions.

sections.heading: Responsibilities

Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Operations | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Receive the Complaint | Employees may raise concerns involving workplace conduct, harassment, discrimination, retaliation, unfair treatment, pay, safety, policy violations or disputed corrective action without fear of retaliation for making a good-faith report or participating in a review. A complaint may be submitted verbally or in writing to the employee's direct supervisor or the Director of Operations. When the concern involves the supervisor or another person in the normal reporting chain, the employee may bypass that person and report directly to the COO or another authorized, conflict-free reviewer. Harassment, discrimination and retaliation reports may also be submitted through the existing employee-portal Google form, including its anonymous reporting option. Anonymous reports will be reviewed, although the lack of identifying or follow-up information may limit the investigation. Nothing in this procedure restricts legally protected communications or reports to appropriate outside authorities.
02 Assign an Impartial Reviewer | The manager receiving a complaint must promptly document the issue, preserve relevant evidence and refer it to an appropriate investigator. Allegations must be reviewed impartially, based on available facts and without assuming either the complaint or the response is automatically correct. Review may include interviews, relevant correspondence, dispatch or system records, witness accounts and the employee's explanation. An accused supervisor or executive must not investigate or make the final decision on a complaint against themselves. Matters involving senior leadership, an owner or another conflict of interest must be directed to an uninvolved authorized leader or an independent outside reviewer, including legal counsel when necessary. Existing complaint-specific reporting and investigation procedures remain in effect and must not be bypassed.
03 Review Complaints and Appeals | Complaints and disciplinary appeals must receive a timely, documented response appropriate to their seriousness. Employees may challenge formal corrective actions, factual findings or disputed management decisions by submitting their explanation and available supporting records through the approved appeal route. The Director of Operations coordinates ordinary complaint and appeal review when not involved in the dispute. Significant discipline, unresolved appeals or management-level conflicts are escalated to the COO when the COO is not implicated; otherwise a conflict-free authorized reviewer must be appointed. The reviewing authority must consider the original evidence, employee response, applicable Corrective Action SOP Version 3.0 provisions, consistency of treatment and any relevant legal protections before confirming, modifying or reversing the decision. Exact appeal deadlines are not established by this SOP and must follow any separately approved procedure and applicable law.
04 Protect Records | Complaint forms, investigation notes, witness statements, corrective actions, employee responses, appeal records and determinations are restricted personnel information. These records must be stored in approved secure company systems, with access limited to authorized personnel who have a legitimate need to know. Confidentiality must be maintained to the extent practical while allowing a fair investigation and required disclosures; absolute secrecy cannot be promised. The Director of Operations coordinates records and retention under applicable requirements and the company's approved retention schedule, without imposing an unconfirmed universal retention period.
05 Communicate and Monitor | Management must document the outcome, notify the affected employee of the decision and any necessary next steps to the extent appropriate, and monitor for retaliation, repeat misconduct or unresolved operational risks. Supervisors must implement authorized corrective measures and report completion. The COO retains executive oversight of significant findings and decisions when not personally involved; suspected retaliation or a conflict within the executive chain must be escalated to a separate authorized reviewer.

content.title: Separation, Final Handoff and Company-Property Return

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Provide a consistent company procedure for separation, final handoff and company-property return.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for separation, final handoff and company-property return. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: All employee separations, including resignations, job abandonment, layoffs and involuntary terminations, must be documented and coordinated through the company's approved offboarding procedure.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current approved instructions; records and reporting channels identified in the procedure; access limited to the assigned role.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Operations | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Approve and Document Separation | All employee separations, including resignations, job abandonment, layoffs and involuntary terminations, must be documented and coordinated through the company's approved offboarding procedure. Department supervisors may accept notice, document performance or conduct concerns and recommend a separation, but may not independently approve or carry out an involuntary termination. The Director of Operations reviews the relevant employment records, applicable Corrective Action SOP Version 3.0 requirements, any employee response and any legal or protected-leave concerns before making a recommendation. The COO must approve involuntary terminations and other major separation decisions before implementation. The approved decision, effective date, reason for separation and responsible managers must be recorded in restricted personnel records.
02 Transfer Active Work | The Director of Operations coordinates the separation with the employee's supervisor, Dispatch, payroll and the personnel responsible for system and facility security. The outgoing employee's active work must be reassigned, including open tow or dispatch calls, VSF responsibilities, customer and property-management issues, pending documentation, sales accounts, keys, schedules and other business commitments applicable to the position. The receiving supervisor must verify that critical records and assignments have been transferred and that no work remains under an unattended account. Employees may not delete records, retain confidential business information or transfer company data to personal accounts as part of departure.
03 Reconcile Assets and Access | A department-specific property checklist must account for company keys, gates and alarm credentials, access cards, fuel or expense cards, phones, tablets, computers, uniforms or protective equipment where applicable, tools, documents and other assigned assets. Items returned, missing, damaged or awaiting collection must be recorded. Access to email, TowCentric, Dialpad, dispatch and VSF systems, company applications, shared files, physical facilities and other restricted resources must be removed or changed promptly at the authorized separation time. For involuntary departures or security-sensitive roles, the Director of Operations must coordinate access changes in advance with the appropriate administrator so permissions can be disabled when the employee is informed, while preserving required company records and any access needed for lawful final-pay or benefits processes. Former employees must not retain shared credentials or use company systems after authorization ends.
04 Supervise Personal-Property Pickup | Employees must have a reasonable, safe opportunity to collect personal belongings. Management may schedule a supervised pickup when security, employee safety or restricted-yard access requires it, and must document any outstanding company or personal property without unnecessary confrontation. Company property concerns must be pursued through lawful return or recovery procedures, not by withholding earned wages or making unauthorized payroll deductions.
05 Complete Final Pay and Closeout | The Director of Operations must coordinate final payroll, approved reimbursements, commissions and applicable benefit or leave balances under the employee's written terms and governing law. Under Texas Labor Code Section 61.014, employees discharged or otherwise involuntarily separated must generally receive final wages no later than six calendar days after discharge, while employees who resign voluntarily must be paid no later than the next regularly scheduled payday; any legally applicable exception or more protective requirement controls. The ordinary Monday payroll-input cutoff does not extend statutory final-pay deadlines. No final paycheck may be conditioned on return of company property. The supervisor and Director of Operations complete the offboarding checklist, document any unresolved issues, confirm access removal and handoff, and report completion or material exceptions to the COO.

content.title: Firearm Retrieval From Impounded Vehicles

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Resolve the remaining decisions for firearm Retrieval From Impounded Vehicles before issuing an operating policy.

sections.heading: Proposed Scope
sections.text: Known or suspected firearms during personal-property retrieval from an impounded vehicle.

sections.heading: Issue Status
sections.text: NOT FOR OPERATIONAL ISSUE. This record preserves the proposed scope and available source direction. Unresolved details are not new permissions, requirements or disciplinary grounds.

sections.heading: Decision to Resolve
sections.text: Approve a safe, lawful firearm-retrieval process, the responding agency, officer-unavailability handling and access to identification or other protected property.

sections.heading: Specific Guidance Required
sections.text:
01. The standalone source requires TCSO; the Dispatch SOP instead says the jurisdiction where the vehicle was impounded. Identify the agency with responsibility for the facility and a verified contact route.
02. The standalone source prohibits all access, even to identification, until an officer arrives and gives no exception or delay limit. Reconcile this with TDLR vehicle-access requirements and obtain an approved fallback when an officer cannot attend.
03. Confirm the lawful notice/appointment process, supervisor authority, emergency response, personal-property documentation and the boundary between officer handling and employee duties. Do not assume an officer will arrive at a promised time.

sections.heading: Existing Source Direction — Not an Issued SOP
sections.text:
Firearm Retrieval Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Purpose To provide a safe, consistent process for retrieving firearms from impounded vehicles while protecting employees, customers, and law enforcement personnel. Scope This procedure applies to all employees handling personal property releases involving a known or suspected firearm. Policy For the safety of all parties, law enforcement must be present during any firearm retrieval from an impounded vehicle. This is a company safety policy and applies to every firearm retrieval, regardless of the circumstances. Procedure 1. Scheduling the Appointment When a customer requests personal property from an impounded vehicle, determine whether a firearm is inside the vehicle. If a firearm is present: * Inform the customer that law enforcement will be present during the retrieval. * Advise the customer that a minimum of one (1) hour notice is required. * Schedule the appointment and document the expected arrival time. 2. Notify Law Enforcement After the appointment has been scheduled, contact the Travis County Sheriff's Office Non-Emergency Dispatch. Provide: * Company name and location * Customer's scheduled appointment time * The reason for the request (firearm retrieval from an impounded vehicle) Law enforcement will coordinate an officer to respond at the scheduled time. 3. Document the Appointment Record the following in TowBook: * Personal Property Release * Firearm Retrieval * Law Enforcement Notified * Appointment Time * Any additional pertinent notes 4. Customer Check-In When the customer arrives: * Verify a valid government-issued photo ID. * Complete the standard personal property release process. * Continue normal release procedures while awaiting law enforcement. 5. Access to the Vehicle If there is a known or suspected firearm inside the vehicle, do not allow the customer to access the vehicle until law enforcement is present. If the customer states their identification is inside the vehicle, they must still wait for law enforcement before entering the storage yard or accessing the vehicle. While customers are generally permitted to retrieve ownership documents or identification, employee safety takes precedence whenever a firearm is involved. 6. Firearm Retrieval Once law enforcement arrives: * Allow the responding officer to manage the firearm retrieval. * Follow any instructions provided by the officer. * Continue processing the personal property release as normal. * Document the items removed from the vehicle and obtain the customer's signature upon completion. Employee Responsibilities Employees are responsible for: * Following this procedure without exception.
* Verifying customer identification. * Coordinating with law enforcement. * Accurately documenting each firearm retrieval. * Maintaining a professional and courteous demeanor throughout the process. Exceptions There are no exceptions to this policy. Any known or suspected firearm inside an impounded vehicle requires law enforcement presence before access to the vehicle is granted. Policy Review This procedure will be reviewed periodically and updated as needed to ensure employee safety and operational consistency.

Billing and Payment Policy – Roadside Use Only 1. Payment Methods: Payments for towing services can be made using credit cards, debit cards, or cash. All payments must be processed through our company's payment processing system to ensure accuracy and accountability.
2. Preferred Payment Method: Customers are required to pay using tap or insert card onsite whenever possible. In cases where card payment is not feasible, customers will pay via a secure payment link provided by the dispatcher.
3. Payment Process: If physical card payments are not feasible, a payment link can be sent to the customer while the vehicle is being towed. At the destination point, the dispatcher will inform the tow truck operator whether the customer has paid for the tow. If payment has not been made, the tow truck operator cannot release the vehicle until payment is received. If payment is not made, the vehicle will be impounded.
4. Issuance of Tow Tickets: All customers must receive a copy of their charges (tow tickets) detailing the services provided and the associated costs.
5. Handling of Cash Payments: Cash payments must be collected directly by the tow truck operator and deposited to an onsite dispatcher. Receipts for cash payments will be issued to the customer upon request.
6. Compliance: Compliance with this Billing and Payment Policy is mandatory for all employees and contractors. Violations may result in disciplinary action, including charges for theft. Top of Form Effective: March 13, 2024. ___________ ______________ _______________ Jerson A. Jendel A.G. Jeidy G.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Confirm Service Eligibility | Apply the source’s 10% military/veteran discount to eligible roadside towing services only. This is not an impound discount or permission to waive regulated charges.
02 Advise the Customer | Tell the customer during the call that proof of military or veteran service must be available for verification. The source recognizes veteran status on a driver’s license or identification, military identification, veteran plates and discharge documentation as examples.
03 Verify and Record the Discount | Have the tow operator verify the qualifying proof, or use an approved verification method with Dispatch. Record the approved discount with the quote and charge record. This SOP does not require copying a military identification card or collecting unnecessary sensitive information.
04 Escalate an Unclear Request | Refer uncertain eligibility, a request for a larger discount or another exception to the Service Manager or authorized management. Employees may not independently promise a different amount.

sections.heading: Existing Source Direction — Not an Issued SOP
sections.text:
English operational source from S12. Provider behavior and permissions below remain subject to the decisions listed above; this is not an issued instruction.
Dispatchers FAQ and Policy for Uber and Lyft Services
Section 1: Preparing for the Rideshare Service General Information How do customers find a safe waiting spot for Uber or Lyft? We recommend customers find a safe and secure spot away from the sun, rain, or cold (inside a building, etc.) while waiting for their ride. Do customers need to download the Uber app? No, customers do not need to download the Uber app. Uber will send them a text message to track their ride, and they will receive an automated phone call from an 800 number with ride details. Dispatchers should only book the Uber after hanging up with the client to ensure they receive the automated phone call. What if a customer needs to walk to the pick-up location? If possible, customers should walk towards the nearest safest pick-up location, as some drivers may not be comfortable picking up passengers from the side of the road. Customers should be cautious of debris, especially at night. Dispatchers reassure customers that Galindo's Towing & Transport has their location and is just a call or text away for assistance. Are rideshare services available during severe weather conditions? Rideshare services are not offered during thunderstorms and snow/ice storms due to low driver availability, potentially causing significant waiting times. This may lead to customers associating long wait times with poor planning, negatively impacting our brand. Is there a preference between Uber and Lyft? Whenever possible, dispatchers should use Lyft over Uber, as Galindo's Towing & Transport benefits from a 5% discount on Lyft pricing.
Payment and Booking Process
How is the additional cost for rideshare services confirmed? Dispatchers must confirm with the customer that they agree to the additional price of the rideshare before scheduling or reserving the service. What if the customer cannot complete full payment on arrival? If the customer cannot complete full payment when the tow truck operator and rideshare service arrive, dispatchers should cancel the rideshare service before or upon their arrival. Although a cancellation fee may apply, it will be substantially less than the full cost of the ride. When should dispatchers book the Uber ride for the customer? Dispatchers should book the Uber ride only after hanging up with the client to ensure they receive the automated phone call from Uber. Section 2: Handling Unavailability and Complaints Alternative Options and Driver Comfort If Uber is unavailable, what should dispatchers do? If, after hanging up with the customer, attempts to book the rideshare result in unavailability, dispatchers should try Lyft or Uber vice versa. If neither has availability, dispatchers should call the customer, informing them of the shortage of service in the area. Alternative transportation arrangements will then be made. Can tow truck operators drive the customer instead? If a tow truck operator feels comfortable driving the customer, it is acceptable, but only if the customer is going to the same location where their vehicle is being dropped off. How can customers tip their rideshare driver?
Customers cannot tip their rideshare driver through their link. If they would like to tip their driver, they can let us know, and we'll send them a separate payment link for them to add a tip. Dispatchers can then go to the rideshare business website and allocate that tip to the driver. What if customers complain about their rideshare driver? In the event of a customer complaint about their rideshare driver, we sincerely apologize for the experience they've gone through. We assure them that we will promptly report the issue to Uber as well. We appreciate their feedback and thank them for reporting the incident. Section 3: Additional Customer Inquiries Driver and Trip Details Can customers request specific rideshare drivers? Customers cannot request specific rideshare drivers as the platform automatically assigns the nearest available driver. What happens if the rideshare driver cancels the trip? If a rideshare driver cancels the trip, dispatchers will be notified, and alternative arrangements will be made promptly, such as rebooking with the same service or trying an alternative rideshare provider. If transportation cannot be secured, refer to question #10. If the tow truck operator says no, then the customer will have to arrange their own transportation. Is there a maximum distance for rideshare services? Rideshare services are generally available within a certain radius. If a customer's destination is outside the usual service area, dispatchers will inform the customer and explore alternative transportation options. Specific Situations and Customer Needs
Can customers bring pets in the rideshare vehicle? Customers should inform dispatchers if they are traveling with pets. While some drivers may accommodate pets, it's essential to check with the rideshare driver beforehand. How can customers track the tow truck's location while waiting for the rideshare? Customers can inquire about the tow truck's location while waiting for the rideshare. Dispatchers will provide updates and ensure a smooth transition between services. Can rideshare services be used for multiple stops? Rideshare services typically allow for one continuous trip. If customers need to make multiple stops, they may need to arrange alternative transportation or discuss options with dispatchers when scheduling. What if a customer left something in the rideshare vehicle? If a customer realizes they left something in the rideshare vehicle, they should contact dispatchers immediately. Dispatchers will assist in communicating with the rideshare driver to retrieve the item if possible. Are rideshare services available 24/7? Rideshare services are generally available 24/7 to us, but availability may vary depending on the location, time, and weather. Dispatchers will inform customers of any potential limitations and explore alternative options if necessary.
Special Requests and Accessibility
Can customers request a specific type of rideshare vehicle (e.g., wheelchair-accessible)? Customers with specific vehicle requirements, such as wheelchair accessibility, should inform dispatchers when scheduling the rideshare service. Efforts will be made to accommodate such requests. Can customers request a specific type of vehicle for their rideshare? Customers can request a specific type of vehicle (e.g., sedan, SUV) by informing the dispatcher during the booking process. While we cannot guarantee availability, we will do our best to accommodate their preferences. Are rideshare services available for long-distance trips? Rideshare services are primarily intended for shorter trips within the local area (30 miles). For long-distance trips, customers should arrange transportation. Can customers request additional assistance from the rideshare driver, such as help with luggage? Customers can request additional assistance from the rideshare driver, such as help with luggage, by communicating their needs during the booking process. Most rideshare drivers are happy to assist with reasonable requests to ensure a comfortable experience for the customer. Top of Form

Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Tow Truck Operator Supervisor | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Verify the Required Credentials | Before operating a company tow truck, verify that the operator has the driver’s license class required for the assigned vehicle and a valid TDLR towing-operator license appropriate for the work.
02 Stay Within License Scope | The source Driver Policy limits Consent Tow operators to consent work; Private Property operators may perform consent and private-property work; Incident Management operators may perform consent, private-property and incident-management work. A license does not itself authorize a particular tow or waive other approvals.
03 Confirm Insurance and Clearance | The driver must be listed on the company insurance policy before operating company vehicles. The responsible supervisor and management must confirm required licensing, insurance eligibility, training and operational clearance before independent duties are assigned. A request to add a driver is not confirmation that coverage is in effect.
04 Report Changes Immediately | Report traffic violations, DUI concerns, license expiration, suspension, restrictions or other changes affecting lawful and safe operation immediately to the supervisor. Do not continue duties that require a missing or invalid qualification.
05 Remove From Affected Work and Review | The supervisor escalates an unconfirmed or restricted qualification to the Director of Operations. Remove the operator from affected work until the required clearance is documented. Corrective action follows HR-CA-017 and the master framework; this SOP does not authorize automatic fines or wage deductions.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Protect People First | When an accident occurs, first address immediate safety and call emergency services when needed. Notify Dispatch or the supervisor as soon as it is safe. Do not remain in an unsafe position merely to obtain photographs.
02 Report and Document | Immediately report the accident, vehicle/property damage or serious complaint. Preserve photographs, video, witness information, tow records and other available facts. Record the location, time, vehicles involved and actions taken without speculating about liability.
03 Coordinate the Investigation | The supervisor notifies the Director of Operations and other required managers. Vehicle damage claims follow CCR-001. Cooperate truthfully with the investigation and preserve original evidence rather than deleting or changing records.
04 Control External Statements | Management handles insurance, legal and settlement communications within its authority. Do not admit fault, promise payment or release restricted evidence without authorization. Insurance disclosure and settlement decisions requiring clarification remain in CCR-003.
05 Keep Recovery and Testing Separate | Customer claim handling must not wait for employee reimbursement discussions. Any testing must follow the adopted written testing program; unconfirmed test triggers and return-to-duty requirements are addressed in TOW-016. Any employee cost recovery follows a separately approved lawful process, not an automatic deduction.

sections.heading: Specific Guidance Required
sections.text:
01. The workbook says release photos “at least 30 minutes” before departure; the Vehicle Damage Claim SOP says “within 30 minutes.” DSP-003 uses the latter explicit source; confirm and correct the conflicting workbook statement.
02. Verify each jurisdiction’s reporting trigger, deadline and required record; do not assume the clock always starts at yard arrival. Define required photos, quality, timing and closeout checks without inventing a photo count.

sections.heading: Existing Source Direction — Not an Issued SOP
sections.text: Towing information such as tow tickets, inputting cars into the impound system, private property software to notify leasing office that a vehicle was towed must be done within the first 2 hours of the vehicle arriving at the VSF. Reporting to the law enfocement jurisidction must be followed. TCSO and APD are within the first 2 hours. Wilco is within the first 30 minutes of the car being picked up, not when the car arrives at the yard. Photos must be taken from all angles including close ups of underneath the vehicle, the front and rear bumper, close ups existing damage such as scratches, dents, missing pieces, photos of the inside of the bed of a truck if the truck bed is exposed. Tow truck operators who fail to take quality and/or quantity of photos of the vehicle and subsequently, a damage claim cannot be deffered back to the original condition of the vehicle, the operator will be responsible for the damages of the vehicle. Upon arrival to the VSF, the dispatcher(s) on duty are responsible for taking new pictures of the vehicle arrival including all angles and pre-existing damages. then they must compare the images taken and the condition of the arrived vehicle to the pictures of taken by the operator before the vehicle was picked up to alert the company of any damages so that proper mitigitation of damages can be made. refer to damage claim SOP. before the vehicle leaves, the dispatchers must take photos of the vehicle at least 30 minutes before the vehicle is picked up.

content.title: Permit-System Mismatch and App Failure Escalation

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Establish consistent responsibilities and steps for permit-system mismatch and app failure escalation.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for permit-system mismatch and app failure escalation. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: A permit mismatch requires preserved evidence and an authorized review, not assumptions or overwritten records.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: TowCentric scan and permit screenshots; complete plate/property; approved support contact; Towbook record.

sections.heading: Source References & Revision History
sections.text:
S01: SOP Approval - Table 1!A102:N102; Guidance Needed!A100:G100
Sources: S01 · S14. Full titles, locations and limitations: Master Index & Source Register.
Revision: October 31, 2026 · 1.0 · November library edition · COO issue review. Full change note: master CSV.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Sales & Development | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Compare the Same Vehicle and Property | Compare the complete license plate, property and relevant times in the driver’s scan with the permit record. Preserve the original screenshot and current permit evidence. Do not assume that a partial plate, different property or minute-only match establishes the same event.
02 Escalate the Same-Minute Conflict | When the driver’s scan shows no permit but the permit appears issued in the same minute, notify the assigned Account Manager and management with the findings. The dispatch source favors leaving the vehicle at the property when possible while the discrepancy is resolved; do not independently create a new tow authorization.
03 Request the Time Detail | Send TowCentric support the subject “Time Differential URGENT.” Identify the property, apartment number when relevant, license plate, scan time and permit time. Ask whether there was a difference in seconds or a system registration delay. Attach the driver’s image and the permit-system screenshot through authorized channels.
04 Obtain an Authorized Decision | If the vehicle is already hooked or towed, record that status and wait for an authorized management direction on the disputed enforcement action. Dispatch and drivers may not silently alter evidence or promise a refund.
05 Retain the Resolution | Keep the support response, verified times, management decision and customer/account follow-up in the appropriate vehicle and property record. Broader system failures also follow ALL-030.

sections.heading: Definitions & Abbreviations
sections.text: PPI: Private Property Impound. PSA: Permit-System Mismatch and App Failure Escalation. SOP: Standard Operating Procedure. HR-CA: Human Resources – Corrective Action.

Reference | When It Applies | Category

HR-CA-020 | Falsifying Records or Evidence | 3 or 4
HR-CA-030 | Poor Communication | 1 to 2 or 3

content.title: Courtesy Releases, Repeat Violations and Account Cost Tracking

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Establish consistent responsibilities and steps for courtesy releases, repeat violations and account cost tracking.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: Account-management and Dispatch personnel handling fee-reduction or courtesy requests from property representatives, residents, visitors or staff.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: Courtesy adjustments depend on the documented cause, repeat-occurrence history and authorized approval; each category has its own schedule.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Written property request; courtesy history; Towbook; approval record; release documentation.

sections.heading: Source References & Revision History
sections.text:
S01: SOP Approval - Table 1!A104:N104; Guidance Needed!A102:G102
Sources: S01 · S06. Full titles, locations and limitations: Master Index & Source Register.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Sales & Development | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Classify and Verify the Request | Identify the cause of the tow and check prior courtesy history for the same type of error, property, staff member, resident or vehicle. A reduced or waived fee does not waive required release documentation. Do not promise an exception outside assigned authority.
02 Leasing-Office Clerical Errors | For repeated occurrences of the same clerical-error type, the first occurrence receives a full courtesy release, the second a 50% reduction, and the third and later occurrences require full payment. Property management must email the explanation, acknowledge its clerical error, request the adjustment and confirm the towing company acted on the property’s supplied information and instructions.
03 Property Staff Vehicles | For staff vehicles, track the individual staff member: first occurrence full courtesy, second 50% reduction, third and later full payment. The history follows the staff member even when another vehicle is used. For a personal or non-business visit, only a one-time 50% reduction may be approved; later occurrences require full payment.
04 New Move-In Registration Failure | When the leasing office failed to register or activate a new resident’s vehicle, the first occurrence may receive a full courtesy release after the required property email and normal release documents. Later tows caused by that resident’s failure to register or confirm registration require full payment; this category has no second courtesy or 50% step. The source does not authorize reimbursement of rideshare, lost wages or inconvenience caused by the leasing-office error.
05 Resident or Visitor Error | When the resident or visitor caused the tow through incorrect registration, an expired permit or another parking violation, full payment is required under ordinary rules. Pressure or dissatisfaction alone does not authorize a courtesy release. Any exception must be recorded as an account-preservation request and approved by management.
06 Account-Preservation Exception | Record the requesting property manager, reason, any threatened pause/cancellation, prior courtesy history, amount waived or reduced and approving person. Account Managers may recommend but may not independently exceed their approval level. Follow DSP-006 for after-hours routing and documentary approval.
07 Record the Adjustment and Transport Decision | Record the approved amount and decision in the vehicle/account history. After a proper no-cost release, free return transport may be arranged only for a towing-company error under the source policy. Do not offer free return transport for property, resident, visitor or staff error. Escalate an inoperable vehicle before quoting or arranging transport.

content.title: Property Complaints, Liability Language and Authorized Communication

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Establish consistent responsibilities and steps for property complaints, liability language and authorized communication.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for property complaints, liability language and authorized communication. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: Client communication must be factual, coordinated and within authority; account pressure does not authorize an exception.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Account contact record; complaint evidence; authorized approval; relevant vehicle record.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Sales & Development | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Separate Account and Operational Ownership | Account Managers and the Director of Sales & Development own existing-client relationships and account concerns. Operational changes must be coordinated with the Director of Operations so Dispatch and drivers receive approved instructions.
02 Document the Complaint | Record the property, requesting representative, affected vehicle or service, facts, supporting communications and desired follow-up. Preserve relevant records and avoid speculation about fault or legality.
03 Do Not Make Unauthorized Commitments | Do not admit company liability, promise a refund or repair payment, authorize a courtesy release, or change patrol/enforcement instructions outside assigned authority. Account-preservation requests follow PPI-009; damage claims follow CCR-001.
04 Protect Account Information | Do not tell residents or guests that the account may be paused or terminated, disclose restricted account discussions, or direct them to pressure the property for a reimbursement. Share internal information only with authorized people who need it.
05 Coordinate and Close the Loop | Communicate an approved resolution through the responsible Account Manager or assigned customer contact. Make sure Operations receives any approved field-service change, and retain the decision and follow-up in the relevant account or claim record.

sections.heading: Definitions & Abbreviations
sections.text: PPI: Private Property Impound. PLC: Property Complaints, Liability Language and Authorized Communication. SOP: Standard Operating Procedure. HR-CA: Human Resources – Corrective Action.

sections.heading: Corrective Action References
sections.text:
Reference | When It Applies | Category
HR-CA-002 | Admitting Fault, Illegality, or Liability | 3
HR-CA-007 | Confidential or Internal Account Information | 3 or 4
HR-CA-009 | Customer Service / Rude Conduct | 1 to 2 or 3
HR-CA-041 | Unauthorized Promise, Discount, Release, or Change | 3
Apply the master framework after fact review. A good-faith report is not misconduct, and one incident must not be divided into artificial multiple write-ups.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Maintain Impartial Relationships | Maintain professional judgment in dealings with property representatives, vendors and other business contacts. Disclose an actual or potential conflict through the supervisor and appropriate management rather than using the relationship for an undisclosed personal benefit.
02 Reject Bribes and Side Payments | Do not request or accept money, gifts, favors, kickbacks or side payments in exchange for a company action. Do not divert company business or use company access, confidential information or opportunities for an undisclosed outside interest.

Follow the approved spending and conflict-of-interest rules; unresolved approval questions go to management.
05 Document the Review | Document the facts and authorized response. Substantiated bribery or kickbacks are reviewed under HR-CA-003; undisclosed conflicts and misuse of opportunities are reviewed under HR-CA-008. Allegations require fact review before discipline.

content.title: Work-Order Intake, Priority, Assignment and Verified Closure

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Provide a consistent company procedure for work-order intake, priority, assignment and verified closure.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for work-order intake, priority, assignment and verified closure. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: All employees may submit a work-order request for facility repairs, equipment defects, vehicle maintenance, supply problems, system issues or other operational work through the company's approved work-request process.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current approved instructions; records and reporting channels identified in the procedure; access limited to the assigned role.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Operations | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Submit the Request | All employees may submit a work-order request for facility repairs, equipment defects, vehicle maintenance, supply problems, system issues or other operational work through the company's approved work-request process. The request should clearly identify the problem, location or affected equipment, the work needed and any immediate operational or safety impact. Supporting photographs or details should be included when useful and appropriate. The initial employee request must remain simple; estimated cost, assigned employee, completion date and other management fields are not required from the person reporting the issue unless that information is already available. Submission does not itself authorize a purchase, vendor engagement or repair.
02 Triage and Assign | The responsible department supervisor or manager reviews each request, determines whether action is required, sets the priority, assigns one accountable owner and establishes a reasonable target for completion. Critical requests involve immediate safety or security hazards, essential equipment failure or a significant interruption of service. High-priority requests materially affect operating capacity or customer obligations but do not require emergency response; routine requests may be scheduled with ordinary maintenance or administrative work. Safety hazards, major truck breakdowns, gate or facility-security failures and other urgent operational interruptions must also be reported immediately by telephone to the on-duty supervisor or Director of Operations under the existing escalation SOP. An electronic work order alone is not sufficient emergency notice.
03 Coordinate and Update | The assigned owner must coordinate the work, provide meaningful status updates, document parts or services needed, identify delays and report changes to the expected completion date. Management must communicate material downtime and arrange qualified coverage, replacement equipment or a safe temporary operating plan when necessary. Department supervisors may approve and assign work only within their delegated operational and purchasing authority. Employees may not commit company funds, authorize repairs or hire vendors without the required approval. Cost estimates, available budget, vendor proposals and any emergency spending must follow the existing company card, purchasing and repair-approval procedures. Expenditures or exceptions beyond approved authority require advance review by the Director of Operations and, when necessary, approval by the COO.
04 Verify Before Closing | A work order may be marked Work Completed when the assigned person reports the work is finished, but it must not be marked Verified Closed until an authorized supervisor or appropriately qualified reviewer confirms the requested work was satisfactorily performed. Verification may include inspection, functional testing, confirmation that equipment is safe to return to service, review of photographs or other appropriate evidence, and reconciliation of any unresolved issues. The person who performed technical work does not alone establish final acceptance when independent or qualified verification is required. Relevant service records, parts, receipts, invoices, actual costs, warranty information and completion notes must be attached or referenced before final closure when applicable.
05 Management Oversight | Department supervisors oversee routine assignments, updates and verification. The Director of Operations monitors overdue and recurring work orders, coordinates priorities across departments, confirms proper escalation and reviews operational or budget exceptions. The COO retains authority over major spending and policy exceptions. Work orders must remain traceable from request through assignment, completion, verification and final closure in the approved company system; this SOP does not establish unconfirmed software, response-time thresholds or dollar approval limits.

content.title: Fleet Preventive Maintenance, Repair Budgets and Readiness

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Provide a consistent company procedure for fleet preventive maintenance, repair budgets and readiness.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for fleet preventive maintenance, repair budgets and readiness. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: All company vehicles and towing equipment must be maintained in safe, reliable operating condition through a documented preventive-maintenance program.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current approved instructions; records and reporting channels identified in the procedure; access limited to the assigned role.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Tow Truck Operator Supervisor | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Maintain Readiness | All company vehicles and towing equipment must be maintained in safe, reliable operating condition through a documented preventive-maintenance program. The maintenance schedule for each unit must account for the chassis manufacturer's recommended service intervals, mileage, engine hours, operating conditions, and the applicable towing equipment manufacturer's inspection and maintenance requirements. Intervals may require adjustment for heavy-duty towing, extended idling, severe use or documented equipment conditions based on qualified guidance. This SOP does not establish unverified mileage or hour intervals; current manufacturer information and approved company schedules control.
02 Inspect and Report | Drivers are responsible for completing required pre-shift and post-shift vehicle and equipment inspections, accurately documenting defects and immediately reporting any condition affecting safe operation. Inspections must address the relevant truck and towing equipment systems, including tires, brakes, lights, fluid leaks, steering, safety equipment, hydraulic lines, winches, attachment points and other items required by the approved checklist. Warning lights, unusual noises, damaged components, leaks, repeated failures or other concerns must be reported to the direct supervisor and Dispatch when availability or active coverage is affected. A truck or piece of equipment presenting a serious safety risk must be removed from service until properly evaluated, corrected as necessary and cleared by qualified personnel. Production requirements and tow quotas do not override this requirement.
03 Schedule Preventive Maintenance | The department supervisor or designated fleet coordinator must track each vehicle's service history, upcoming maintenance, reported defects, open repairs, expected downtime and readiness status in the approved fleet or work-order records. Records must distinguish chassis service from maintenance or repair of the Jerr-Dan towing equipment where applicable. Completed oil and filter changes, brake and tire work, hydraulic maintenance, inspections, service bulletins, warranty repairs and other work must be recorded with service dates, odometer or engine-hour readings when relevant, parts, labor, vendor information, receipts and follow-up requirements. Recurring defects or abnormal maintenance spending must be flagged for review instead of repeatedly treated as isolated repairs.
04 Approve and Document Repairs | Routine service appointments and downtime are coordinated by the responsible supervisor with Dispatch and the Director of Operations to maintain safe coverage and appropriate vehicle assignments. Nonroutine repairs require a documented assessment or estimate and authorization under the company's purchasing and repair-approval procedures before work begins, except where an approved emergency process applies. Department budgets are established by the COO, and the Director of Operations monitors actual maintenance costs, repair needs and available funds within those approved budgets. Major expenses, purchases exceeding delegated limits and exceptions outside the approved budget require COO approval. No employee may independently commit company funds or authorize a vendor beyond their assigned authority.
05 Verify Return to Service | A completed repair does not automatically restore a vehicle to active service. A supervisor or appropriately qualified reviewer must confirm that the required work is complete and that any necessary functional tests, safety checks and documentation have been performed. Technical repairs must be verified by qualified personnel when the component or defect requires it. Only after that review may the truck's status be changed from out of service to available. The Director of Operations oversees overall fleet readiness, preventive-maintenance compliance, downtime, repair cost trends and recommendations regarding continued repair versus equipment replacement, with material budget or fleet decisions escalated to the COO.
