content.title: Repair Approval, Vendor Handoff and Payment After Verification

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Provide a consistent company procedure for repair approval, vendor handoff and payment after verification.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for repair approval, vendor handoff and payment after verification. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: Nonroutine repairs to company vehicles, towing equipment, facilities, security systems and other business assets must be documented through the approved work-order or maintenance process before a vendor is engaged or work is authorized, except where an approved emergency response is necessary.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current approved instructions; records and reporting channels identified in the procedure; access limited to the assigned role.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Service Manager | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Document the Repair Need | Nonroutine repairs to company vehicles, towing equipment, facilities, security systems and other business assets must be documented through the approved work-order or maintenance process before a vendor is engaged or work is authorized, except where an approved emergency response is necessary. The request must identify the defect or required work, affected asset, operational impact and any immediate safety concern. The responsible supervisor must evaluate the need, determine whether the asset should remain out of service and obtain a written estimate whenever reasonably possible. Estimates should identify the proposed repair, parts, labor, anticipated total cost, expected completion time and any material exclusions or warranty considerations. A work-order request or vendor estimate is not itself permission to spend company funds.
02 Approval and Budget Limits | Supervisors may approve routine repairs only within their expressly delegated purchasing authority and the approved department budget. The Director of Operations reviews operational necessity, reasonable costs, available alternatives, proposed downtime and maintenance history, and coordinates approvals across departments. The COO establishes budget authority and must approve major repair expenses, work outside approved budgets, commitments above delegated limits and significant financial exceptions before the company is committed. No employee may independently authorize a vendor, issue an unrestricted purchase order, approve additional parts or promise payment beyond their assigned authority. This SOP does not create unconfirmed dollar limits; existing written approvals and the company's purchasing policy control.
03 Urgent Safety-Critical Work | For a safety-critical breakdown or another urgent interruption that cannot reasonably wait for the normal process, the employee must immediately telephone the on-duty supervisor or Director of Operations and identify the risk and minimum work needed. Management must seek authorization from the appropriate decision-maker as quickly as circumstances permit, limit any emergency commitment to what is necessary to make the situation safe or restore essential operations, and record the reason, contacted approver, cost information and decision. Emergency circumstances do not automatically waive spending controls or permit unnecessary additional repairs. Unsafe vehicles or equipment must remain out of service until adequately repaired and cleared by qualified personnel.
04 Vendor Handoff | Once a repair is authorized, the assigned manager must provide the vendor with the approved scope, affected vehicle or equipment details, known symptoms, approved estimate or cost ceiling when applicable, expected communications and required completion evidence. Any new defect, scope change, added labor, replacement part, material cost increase or unexpected delay must be reported to management before additional chargeable work proceeds. Revised work and pricing require authorization at the appropriate level; a vendor may not treat the original approval as blanket permission for additional work. The assigned owner tracks work status, parts delays, downtime, warranty eligibility and the estimated return-to-service date, and coordinates changes affecting Dispatch or other operating departments.
05 Acceptance and Payment | The vendor's statement that a repair is finished does not alone establish acceptance or authorize unrestricted final payment. The responsible supervisor must obtain the service details and arrange suitable inspection, functional checks and safety verification by appropriately qualified personnel, particularly for braking, steering, hydraulic, electrical, towing or other safety-sensitive systems. Incomplete or defective work must be documented and returned for correction or warranty review before final acceptance when permitted by the contract. The invoice must be reconciled against the approved estimate, any approved changes, work actually completed, parts and labor documentation, applicable warranties and receipts. Deposits or contractual progress payments are allowed only when specifically approved and documented; final payment authorization follows satisfactory verification, approved invoice review and the company's established accounts-payable authority, subject to any binding contractual or legal payment obligations.
06 Oversight and Closeout | Department supervisors manage routine work and completion checks. The Director of Operations oversees repair priorities, vendor coordination, cost review, safety acceptance, recurring failures and the documentation necessary for payment review. The COO approves major expenditures, material disputes and exceptions beyond delegated authority. The work order and related fleet or facility records must retain the approvals, estimate, revisions, invoices, supporting evidence, inspection results, payment disposition and verified closure.

content.title: Facility Inspections, Supplies and Recurring Service Schedule

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Provide a consistent company procedure for facility inspections, supplies and recurring service schedule.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for facility inspections, supplies and recurring service schedule. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: Company offices, vehicle-storage facilities, tow yards, parking areas, gates, storage spaces, restrooms and other operating areas must be maintained in a clean, safe and serviceable condition.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current approved instructions; records and reporting channels identified in the procedure; access limited to the assigned role.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Service Manager | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Inspection and Facility Coverage | Company offices, vehicle-storage facilities, tow yards, parking areas, gates, storage spaces, restrooms and other operating areas must be maintained in a clean, safe and serviceable condition. Employees are responsible for promptly reporting damaged property, unsafe conditions, inadequate supplies and sanitation concerns, and for completing the housekeeping duties assigned to their shifts under the existing housekeeping SOP. The responsible supervisor must complete or assign a documented baseline facility inspection at least weekly, with additional checks whenever a specific hazard, weather event, equipment condition or operating requirement warrants them. Inspections should address applicable gates and fencing, access paths, lighting, plumbing, electrical concerns, drainage, surfaces, storage areas, offices, restrooms, portable toilets, landscaping and other facility conditions. This SOP does not establish unconfirmed specialist inspection intervals or replace inspections required by law, equipment instructions or a qualified vendor.
02 Report and Triage Defects | Facility defects and nonurgent maintenance needs must be entered into the approved work-order process with a clear description, location, operational impact and useful photographs when available. The supervisor assigns one responsible owner, establishes priority and follows the request through completion and verification. Serious hazards, including exposed electrical components, structural concerns, major plumbing failures, inaccessible gates or conditions threatening facility security or employee safety, require immediate telephone escalation to the on-duty supervisor or Director of Operations. Employees must not attempt repairs involving electrical, structural, hazardous-material or other specialized risks beyond their training and authority. Affected areas or equipment must be secured or removed from use when safe to do so until qualified personnel assess the condition.
03 Recurring Service Calendar | The responsible supervisor maintains an approved recurring-service calendar covering the services actually used at each location, which may include portable-toilet service, waste removal, routine cleaning, landscaping, pest control, plumbing or building maintenance and other vendor-supported work. Each scheduled service must have an assigned company contact, the authorized vendor or provider, its agreed service scope and frequency, and a method for documenting completion. Supervisors must follow up on missed visits, repeated service problems or deficiencies and confirm satisfactory performance before approving the associated invoice for payment review. Vendor scopes, service frequencies and contracts must be confirmed from current company records rather than assumed or created through this SOP.
04 Weekly Supply Checks | Department supervisors must inspect and monitor essential operating supplies at least weekly, consistent with the existing housekeeping procedure. This includes restroom and sanitation materials, cleaning products, office consumables, trash supplies, suitable safety-related supplies and other items needed for continuous operations. Supervisors establish practical minimum stock quantities based on usage and replenishment lead time, report shortages before supplies are exhausted and coordinate authorized restocking. Items requiring specialized handling or protective equipment must be managed by qualified personnel. Employees must not use unapproved chemicals, improvise unsafe substitutions or purchase supplies outside their delegated authority.
05 Purchasing and Verification | Routine supplies, service contracts, repairs and contractor work remain subject to the company's existing purchasing and work-order procedures. Department supervisors may request or approve expenses only within their authorized spending limits and approved budgets. The Director of Operations monitors facility inspection results, outstanding work orders, stock availability, recurring-service compliance, vendor performance and related costs across departments. Major purchases, changes outside approved budgets, new contractual commitments and significant exceptions require COO approval. Inspection checklists, inventory requests, service records, work orders, receipts, invoices and verified completion notes must be retained in the approved company records so unresolved conditions remain traceable and accountable.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Provide a consistent company procedure for gate, camera, key and alarm security.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for gate, camera, key and alarm security. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: Company gates, locks, keys, access credentials, alarm systems, cameras and other facility security controls must be managed to protect employees, customers, stored vehicles, equipment and restricted company information.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current approved instructions; records and reporting channels identified in the procedure; access limited to the assigned role.

sections.heading: Source References & Revision History

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Service Manager | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Security and Access Controls | Company gates, locks, keys, access credentials, alarm systems, cameras and other facility security controls must be managed to protect employees, customers, stored vehicles, equipment and restricted company information. Entry to the vehicle-storage facility, tow yard, offices, secure storage and other controlled areas is limited to employees, approved contractors and visitors who have an authorized business purpose. Employees may access only the spaces and systems required for their assigned duties. Granting physical entry to a visitor, customer or vendor does not authorize access to stored vehicles or waive the company's separate VSF identification, ownership verification, documentation and vehicle-release requirements. Visitors and vendors must use the approved entry process, remain within authorized areas and be escorted or supervised where the work or security conditions require it.
02 Access Register | The Director of Operations maintains or designates a custodian for a controlled security-access register identifying assigned physical keys, gate remotes or codes, access cards, alarm permissions, camera-system accounts and authorized administrators. Supervisors request access based on specific job responsibilities; only designated administrators may issue, modify or revoke restricted permissions. Credentials must be individual where supported and may not be shared, copied, posted in general Slack channels or provided to an unauthorized person. Department transfers, changes in responsibility, lost credentials and employee departures require prompt review of all related permissions. During separation, access removal and recovery of issued assets must be coordinated with the approved offboarding procedure and timed to protect facility security without disrupting required record preservation.
03 Routine Function Checks | Assigned supervisors must routinely verify that gates close and secure properly, locks and access controls function, alarm faults are reported, and cameras or recording systems provide the coverage and system status expected under the approved equipment checklist. A documented facility review must be included in the established inspection process, with additional checks when failures or security concerns occur. Recording access, footage retrieval, copying and disclosure are restricted to authorized personnel with a legitimate company purpose. Employees may not alter, delete, distribute or use camera footage for personal purposes. Incident recordings and access logs potentially relevant to a complaint, damage claim, theft or legal matter must be preserved through the approved evidence and records process; routine retention periods must follow the actual configured system and company-approved retention policy rather than an unconfirmed number of days.
04 Security Incident Response | Missing keys, compromised codes, suspected unauthorized entry, malfunctioning cameras, an unsecured gate, alarm failures and any threat to custody of stored vehicles require prompt notification to the on-duty supervisor. A significant or active security failure requires an immediate telephone call under the company's urgent-escalation policy; Slack or a work-order ticket alone is not sufficient. Supervisors must assess the risk, restrict unsafe or unauthorized access when feasible, coordinate an approved temporary security or monitoring plan and contact the responsible system administrator or qualified service vendor. Emergency response or law enforcement must be contacted when circumstances warrant it. Lost or compromised access must be disabled or changed as soon as practical through authorized personnel, and no employee may bypass security controls or improvise access procedures without approval.
05 Records and Access Changes | All security incidents, issued or recovered credentials, permission changes, system failures, affected equipment, temporary measures and corrective work must be documented in the appropriate restricted company record or work order. After a repair or access change, the responsible supervisor or qualified administrator verifies the required security function before marking the issue resolved. Supervisors oversee routine site checks and authorized visitor entry. The Director of Operations oversees the access register, incident investigation, technical coordination and cross-department security readiness. The COO approves major security expenditures and exceptions beyond delegated authority. The current administrators, key and code custody arrangements, approved backup procedures, vendor contacts and camera retention settings must be recorded in a restricted operational directory rather than invented or exposed in this SOP.

content.title: Weather Readiness, Generators and Building Supplies

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Provide a consistent company procedure for weather readiness, generators and building supplies.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for weather readiness, generators and building supplies. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: The company must maintain reasonable readiness for severe weather, power outages and other conditions that could affect the tow yard, vehicle-storage facility, offices, fleet or employee safety.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current approved instructions; records and reporting channels identified in the procedure; access limited to the assigned role.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Service Manager | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Readiness and Ownership | The company must maintain reasonable readiness for severe weather, power outages and other conditions that could affect the tow yard, vehicle-storage facility, offices, fleet or employee safety. The Director of Operations monitors credible weather alerts and coordinates preparation with the responsible supervisors and Dispatch. Before anticipated storms, flooding, high winds, freezing temperatures or extended power interruptions, supervisors must conduct or assign a documented site readiness check appropriate to the forecast and affected locations. This includes gates and fences, drainage and standing-water risks, roof or building concerns visible from safe access points, exposed equipment and materials, outdoor lighting, vehicle positioning, emergency access routes and other conditions that could compromise property security or operating continuity. Employees must not climb, enter unstable structures or perform specialized inspections beyond their training or authority.
02 Supplies and Preparation | Supervisors must ensure that appropriate weather and outage supplies are available for the actual facility and work performed. This may include working flashlights, batteries, suitable rain gear, approved emergency lighting, first-aid materials, communication equipment, absorbent or cleanup supplies and other necessary items. Supplies must be checked during facility-readiness reviews and shortages reported before they interrupt operations. The Director of Operations coordinates replenishment under the company's existing purchasing procedure; the COO retains approval authority over major expenses, budget exceptions and new equipment commitments. Exact quantities, locations and equipment lists must be based on the facility's verified needs rather than arbitrary amounts established here.
03 Generator Controls | Where the company has a generator, backup power equipment or related fuel supplies, they must be identified in an equipment register and maintained, inspected and tested in accordance with the actual manufacturer's instructions, installation requirements and applicable safety standards. Only trained or qualified personnel may operate, inspect or service the equipment to the extent of their authorization. Generators must never be operated inside a building, garage, shed or other enclosed or partially enclosed area where exhaust can accumulate. Portable equipment must be placed outdoors with appropriate separation from doors, windows, vents and occupied spaces, consistent with manufacturer and safety requirements. Fuel must be stored in approved containers and locations, secured from ignition sources and handled only by authorized personnel. Electrical connections must use properly rated, undamaged equipment and any building connection must be installed and managed by a qualified electrician through an approved transfer or interconnection system; employees must never backfeed a building through an ordinary receptacle or improvise wiring. This SOP does not assume a generator is present or establish an unverified model, capacity, fuel type, fuel quantity or testing frequency.
04 Response and Continuity | When dangerous conditions develop, supervisors coordinate necessary staffing, Dispatch coverage, secured vehicle positioning, VSF access and release continuity, safe communications and appropriate changes to towing or yard assignments. Employees must promptly report flooding, dangerous driving conditions, lightning exposure, falling debris, electrical hazards, structural damage, loss of security systems or other significant risks. Production goals do not override the existing stop-work and safety-reporting SOP. An employee with a reasonable good-faith safety concern must stop the affected work, move to safety when necessary and immediately notify the supervisor and Dispatch when service is affected. Serious incidents, hazardous conditions and major outages require immediate telephone escalation through the approved on-call chain, with emergency services contacted when warranted. Temporary operating or manual procedures require authorized management approval and must protect vehicle custody, customer records and employee safety.
05 Post-Event Inspection | After a storm or interruption, the assigned supervisor must complete a documented post-event inspection of affected access routes, gates, fencing, buildings, standing-water areas, electrical or backup-power systems, vehicles and towing equipment before normal use resumes. Suspected electrical, structural or mechanical hazards must remain isolated or out of service pending assessment and clearance by appropriately qualified personnel. Damage, supply use, service interruption, temporary measures, corrective work and verified restoration must be recorded in the appropriate incident or work-order system. The Director of Operations oversees preparation, continuity, inspection follow-up and recovery priorities; the COO approves major expenditures and exceptions beyond delegated authority. The approved emergency contacts, supply inventory, generator-specific operating instructions and readiness checklists must be maintained separately and updated when actual equipment or facility conditions change.

content.title: Emergency Equipment Register, Inspections and Training Calendar

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Provide a consistent company procedure for emergency equipment register, inspections and training calendar.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for emergency equipment register, inspections and training calendar. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: The company must maintain an accurate emergency-equipment register for each operating location and vehicle where emergency or safety equipment is provided or required.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Current approved instructions; records and reporting channels identified in the procedure; access limited to the assigned role.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Director of Operations | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Maintain the Register | The company must maintain an accurate emergency-equipment register for each operating location and vehicle where emergency or safety equipment is provided or required. The register must identify the actual equipment on hand, its location, type or identifying details when applicable, the responsible department or assigned custodian, required inspection or servicing arrangements, and its current condition or readiness status. Equipment may include first-aid kits, fire extinguishers, automated external defibrillators (AEDs), eyewash equipment, emergency lighting, spill-response materials and other protective or emergency supplies when applicable to the location, hazards and legal requirements. This SOP does not assume that every listed item is installed or required at every location; actual needs must be verified against applicable rules, site conditions and approved safety assessments.
02 Inspect and Check Stock | The responsible supervisor must assign an employee or qualified service provider to check that emergency equipment is present, identifiable, readily accessible, free from obstruction and in serviceable condition. Inspection, servicing, testing, replacement and certification schedules must follow the requirements applicable to the particular equipment, manufacturer instructions and any governing code or regulation. Required technical testing, extinguisher servicing, AED maintenance or other specialized work must be performed by appropriately trained or qualified personnel. No employee may represent an unperformed inspection as completed, alter certification records or perform technical servicing beyond their qualifications. The Director of Operations coordinates the central inspection and service calendar and confirms that responsibilities and due dates are assigned rather than allowing items to lapse without an owner.
03 Report Deficiencies | Employees must immediately notify their supervisor when emergency supplies are missing, depleted, used, damaged, discharged, expired, inaccessible or otherwise not ready. The supervisor must evaluate the safety impact, arrange an authorized replacement or qualified service, and implement reasonable temporary precautions or restrict affected work when necessary. Equipment used during an incident must be promptly inspected and replenished or serviced before being marked ready for use again. Serious deficiencies that create an immediate hazard or leave employees without required safety protection must be escalated by telephone under the company's safety and stop-work reporting policy; an ordinary supply or maintenance ticket alone is not sufficient for an active emergency.
04 Training and Competency | Training requirements must be based on actual employee responsibilities, expected response duties, installed equipment, applicable law and the approved emergency-response procedures. Supervisors must identify employees who require equipment orientation, first-aid or CPR/AED training, fire-extinguisher training or other role-specific instruction, as applicable. The Director of Operations must maintain a training calendar showing completion dates, instructors or providers where required, competency or certifications obtained and renewal dates when applicable. Employees may not be directed to conduct emergency procedures beyond their training or attempt actions that expose them to unnecessary danger. In an emergency, employees must contact 911 when appropriate, protect their own safety and follow the separately approved medical, fire, evacuation or electrical response procedures; this inventory SOP does not establish clinical or technical emergency-treatment instructions.
05 Verify and Update Records | Supervisors must document each required inspection, corrective finding, replacement request, service completion and equipment use in the approved company records. The Director of Operations maintains oversight of emergency-equipment readiness across the VSF, offices, yard, company vehicles and other applicable work locations, and coordinates qualified vendors, training and recurring reviews. Purchases and service contracts follow existing delegated spending limits and approved budgets. Major purchases, financial exceptions and changes beyond departmental authority require COO approval. Equipment-specific inspection frequencies, service vendors, actual inventory, certification requirements and response instructions must be confirmed and maintained in the controlled equipment register and related approved procedures rather than invented or assumed in this SOP.

sections.heading: Purpose

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: The assigned personnel and supervisors responsible for card use, purchasing limits and expense categorization. The procedure applies to the work and handoffs described below, within each role’s authority.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Assigned Personnel | Carry out the steps within the scope of the assigned role; report concerns and preserve required records.
Chief Operating Officer | Coordinate the policy within assigned authority; use the procedure’s stated review, approval and escalation requirements.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Authorize the Card and Limit | The employee must sign the card authorization form before access is granted. Establish the assigned limit according to job duties and anticipated expenses, with required funds available. The legacy form’s $2,000 daily limit is specific to that assignment; it does not replace the current role-based approval process.
02 Approve Business Purchases | Use company cards only for approved business purposes and within the assigned limit and department budget. Obtain the required supervisor or management approval before purchase. Personal purchases and cash advances are prohibited.
03 Submit Receipts and Business Purpose | Submit an itemized receipt, purchase description and approving supervisor’s name through the approved process. The card-use source requires receipts within the same business week or when requested. Be available to explain transactions flagged during reconciliation.
04 Secure the Card and Report Problems | Keep the card secure and do not share it with unauthorized people. Immediately report a lost, stolen or compromised card, missing receipt, disputed charge or suspected misuse to the supervisor and Director of Operations.
05 Reconcile and Review Misuse | Supervisors verify authorization, necessity and categorization. The Director of Operations coordinates records and review. Corrective action may include loss of card access or other authorized action. Reimbursement or wage recovery is not automatic and must follow a separately authorized lawful process under CCR-002.

content.title: Vehicle Damage Claim Intake, Investigation & Response

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Establish consistent responsibilities and steps for vehicle Damage Claim Intake, Investigation & Response.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: Dispatch, towing personnel, account-management contacts, the claims team and managers handling reported vehicle damage. This workflow does not authorize release delays, payroll deductions or an insurance-disclosure decision.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: Report promptly, preserve evidence, investigate fairly and communicate an authorized resolution. Making the customer whole and documenting the claim take priority over a separate worker-recovery discussion.

sections.heading: Supplies & Equipment
sections.text: Damage-claim sheet; Towbook record; timestamped photos; preserved footage; repair estimate; management contact list.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Dispatch / Dispatch Manager | Capture condition evidence, receive the claim and make the immediate claims-team handoff.
Samuel — Towing Operations Manager | Investigate, preserve findings and develop the repair plan.
Austin — Director of Operations | Review cost and purchasing approval; receive invoices and mitigation costs.
Alex / Jeidy / Jarif | Handle the assigned customer communications and retain written follow-up.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Photograph and Report | Dispatch photographs the vehicle on arrival and within 30 minutes before departure. If damage is spotted or reported, the dispatcher immediately contacts the assigned Dispatch Manager. Preserve the tow record, original photographs and available yard, truck or property footage.
02 Notify the Claims Team | When the Dispatch Manager is available, that manager contacts all three: Alex, Director of Sales & Development; Austin, Director of Operations; and Samuel, Towing Operations Manager. If the assigned manager is unavailable or off duty, Dispatch may contact any one of those three directly. The claims team advises ownership.
03 Receive the Customer Claim | Provide the damage-claim sheet and explain that the submission goes directly to management. Record the first report time, vehicle, alleged damage, customer contact details and supplied evidence. Acknowledge the concern without promising fault, a repair amount or an unapproved settlement.
04 Investigate and Share Findings | Samuel investigates and supplies Alex and Jarif with findings and evidence supporting fault or no fault. An assessment may require a visit to the vehicle. Document its condition with detailed timestamped photographs and identify the part, mounting damage or other repair issue. Preserve contrary evidence as well as evidence supporting the company.
05 Prepare a Costed Repair Plan | When company-caused damage is confirmed, coordinate the plan with Austin and Samuel. Identify the part, availability and delivery, labor or shop needs, anticipated total cost and realistic repair timeline. Austin reviews and approves expenditure; Alex communicates the proposed plan. Customer resolution is separate from a worker-reimbursement discussion.
06 Meet the Response Standard | The original workflow requires same-day repair planning and customer communication when the company is at fault. When the evidence supports no company fault, communicate the denial within three days of the customer’s first report. A deadline does not prove fault or justify an unsupported denial; escalate incomplete findings and keep the customer informed.
07 Use the Assigned Customer Contact | English-language customer communication is assigned to Alex. Spanish-language communication when the company is at fault is assigned to Jeidy, Dispatch Department Leader. Spanish-language no-fault denials are assigned to Jarif, Account Manager. The assigned Account Manager relays communications concerning their own account. Follow each telephone call with an email to preserve the record.
08 Close the Claim and Maintain the Documents | Send receipts, repair invoices and mitigation costs to Austin for financial planning and claim records. If driver fault is found, notify the driver’s supervisor; recovery is handled separately under CCR-002. Route law-firm caller details and callback information to the Director of Operations. Update the written SOP and companion flowchart together when approved responsibilities change.

sections.heading: Related Decisions & Boundaries
sections.text: CCR-002, CCR-003 and CCR-004 are guidance drafts, not operating authorization. The preserved flowchart assigns roles and response targets; it does not authorize a payroll deduction, an unlawful release delay or an unapproved insurance position.

content.title: Employee Damage Recovery & Payroll Deductions

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Resolve the remaining decisions for employee Damage Recovery & Payroll Deductions before issuing an operating policy.

sections.heading: Proposed Scope
sections.text: Proposed recovery of vehicle, equipment, technology, card and other losses from an employee or contractor.

sections.heading: Issue Status
sections.text: NOT FOR OPERATIONAL ISSUE. This record preserves the proposed scope and available source direction. Unresolved details are not new permissions, requirements or disciplinary grounds.

sections.heading: Decision to Resolve
sections.text: Approve a separate, legally reviewed recovery agreement and decision process before deductions or offsets are used.

sections.heading: Specific Guidance Required
sections.text:
01. Legacy sources impose automatic pay-cycle deductions, escrow recovery, fines or legal costs. Current ALL-021 and MGT-016 prohibit automatic or unauthorized wage recovery. Confirm which provisions are withdrawn or replaced.
02. Distinguish employees from genuine independent contractors and determine applicable authorization, wage/overtime/salary protections and final-pay requirements. A policy acknowledgment alone must not be assumed sufficient for every deduction.
03. Define investigation of responsibility, evidence, written notice, employee response, actual supported loss, approval, any separate agreement, ledger and dispute process. Do not withhold earned final pay until property is returned.
04. Reconcile the technology policy’s 10-day replacement option with the equipment policy’s same-pay-period language; identify any existing valid escrow agreements rather than assuming an escrow exists.

sections.heading: Existing Source Direction — Not an Issued SOP
sections.text:
S03 proposes immediate authorized-escrow recovery, or the nearest pay cycle/payment plan where no escrow exists. S08/S09 impose repair or replacement deductions even for accidental damage. S05 proposes next-paycheck recovery of unauthorized card charges. These provisions are preserved as review issues, not issued payroll instructions.
Source-specific recovery clauses: the equipment policy covers intentional or accidental damage other than normal wear and proposes same-pay-period repair/replacement deductions, with equal make/model replacement before deduction. The technology policy instead allows replacement with an equal make/model within 10 days, after written notice of intent. The driver and equipment policies also purport to shift all company legal expenses for recovery litigation to the worker. None of those clauses is issued as automatic authority in this library.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Supervisor | Address immediate risk, preserve evidence, document facts and obtain the employee’s response.
Director of Operations | Review the code, category, consistency and proposed formal action.
COO / Uninvolved Executive | Approve suspension, termination and other decisions reserved to executive authority; resolve conflicts of interest.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Identify the Concern | Missing a scheduled shift without required notice. A pattern is Category 2; abandoning a critical shift or causing serious operational exposure may be Category 3.
02 Use the Normal Classification | Normal category: 2 or 3. Usual starting response: Documented or written warning; final warning or termination review when serious or repeated. These are usual responses, not guaranteed steps or an automatic finding.
03 Verify Before Deciding | An allegation is not a finding. Preserve relevant records, identify witnesses and review the employee’s training, explanation, active history, intent, actual impact and foreseeable risk. Protect applicable leave, accommodation, good-faith reporting and other legal rights.
04 Obtain the Required Review | The Director of Operations reviews formal corrective action. Escalate serious Category 3 or 4 matters. Suspension, termination and other reserved decisions require COO approval before implementation; an implicated reviewer must be replaced by an uninvolved authorized reviewer.
05 Document, Communicate and Follow Up | Record the applicable code and final category, objective facts, evidence, employee response, approved action, required improvement, deadline/support and follow-up. Meet privately, provide a copy and request acknowledgment of receipt. A refusal to sign is not proof of guilt. Do not divide one incident into artificial multiple write-ups.

sections.text: This preserves the existing misconduct reference and review framework; it does not finalize the conflicting attendance/no-show/probation ladder proposals held in ALL-004, ALL-008 and ALL-022.

sections.heading: Procedure

content.title: Unauthorized Visitors, Passengers, or Restricted-Area Access

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Identify the conduct covered by HR-CA-043 and the review required before corrective action is selected.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: Conduct described in this policy reference, reviewed under the company-wide corrective-action framework.

sections.heading: Policy Standard
sections.text: Allowing an unauthorized visitor or passenger into a Company vehicle, work area, yard, office, restricted area, or other controlled location.

sections.heading: Normal Category & Usual Starting Response
sections.text: Category 2 or 3. Remove the unauthorized person and document the event; Category 3 when safety, security, customer property, or Company liability is exposed.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.text:
Supervisor | Address immediate risk, preserve evidence, document facts and obtain the employee’s response.
Director of Operations | Review the code, category, consistency and proposed formal action.
COO / Uninvolved Executive | Approve suspension, termination and other decisions reserved to executive authority; resolve conflicts of interest.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text:
01 Identify the Concern | Allowing an unauthorized visitor or passenger into a Company vehicle, work area, yard, office, restricted area, or other controlled location.
02 Use the Normal Classification | Normal category: 2 or 3. Usual starting response: Remove the unauthorized person and document the event; Category 3 when safety, security, customer property, or Company liability is exposed. These are usual responses, not guaranteed steps or an automatic finding.
03 Verify Before Deciding | An allegation is not a finding. Preserve relevant records, identify witnesses and review the employee’s training, explanation, active history, intent, actual impact and foreseeable risk. Protect applicable leave, accommodation, good-faith reporting and other legal rights.
04 Obtain the Required Review | The Director of Operations reviews formal corrective action. Escalate serious Category 3 or 4 matters. Suspension, termination and other reserved decisions require COO approval before implementation; an implicated reviewer must be replaced by an uninvolved authorized reviewer.
05 Document, Communicate and Follow Up | Record the applicable code and final category, objective facts, evidence, employee response, approved action, required improvement, deadline/support and follow-up. Meet privately, provide a copy and request acknowledgment of receipt. A refusal to sign is not proof of guilt. Do not divide one incident into artificial multiple write-ups.
